## 84. Block 12 on the desktop: the window was in session 0, and `VirtualLock` does not pin a frame

Written 2026-10-15, on branch `block12-session1`. Two items: the nine harness
failures of that morning's `wc-guest.sh all`, and Block 12, the cross-VM damage
leg that had never scrolled anything.

### 84.1 Status in one paragraph

**Firefox on the guest's compositor, scrolled 60 notches on the real desktop,
over 498 verified commits with 0 stale.** That is
`scripts/wc-desktop.sh damage`, run at 14:21–14:24: 17 passed, 0 failed. Two
findings got it there, both measured. First, the old hypothesis held: the leg's
window was in **session 0**, where Firefox's `HWND` has `WS_VISIBLE` set and
`IsWindowVisible` still says no. Second, and nobody had predicted it, once the
page did scroll **59 of 535 commits were stale, each by exactly one 4 KiB
page**. The cause is that a `VirtualLock`ed arena does not keep its physical
frames on this guest. The arena is now large pages first. The nine harness
failures are fixed and `wc-guest.sh all` reads **72 passed, 0 failed**. The
section ends with an incident (84.7): during the last control run, on the old
`VirtualLock` path, the guest hard-hung and was reset.

### 84.2 Nine failures, none of them the compositor's

`wc-guest.sh all` at 64 passed, 9 failed (`/tmp/wcrun/sv-wc-guest.log`). Every
failure was the harness:

| check | cause | fix |
|---|---|---|
| block 4 "smithay globals" | greps `5 globals advertised`; the compositor advertises 16 | asserts the handshake and `wl_compositor`, `wl_subcompositor`, `wl_shm`, `xdg_wm_base`, `wl_seat` by name |
| block 4 fragmented, 4 checks | read the server log 2 s after the client exited, while the relay was still dripping 372 bytes at about 200 B/s; the same log, read later, had every milestone | `relayed()` waits for the server's own `client … disconnected` (bounded, 30 s) |
| block 9 `term` | asks for a FILE arena; the compositor refuses one on a real VM (§28.2) | leg removed; the driver refuses `arena` by name; `termg` is the same client over guest RAM |
| block 9 `termf`/`pres`/`termg` pool growth, empty FAIL | positional regex; stage 16 added `reclaimed`/`republished` | fields read by name, here and in `wc-launch.sh`; `10 overflows)` no longer passes as zero |

Also: `wc-guest.sh`, `wc-desktop.sh`, `wc-titlebar.sh` and `wc-popup.sh`
resolved a `GUEST` default and exported nothing, so `wc_topology_declare
cross-vm` refused unless the caller had set `WC_GUEST`. All seven harnesses that
default it now export it. `ROOTC` survives a multi-word value: three scripts
piped into `"$ROOTC"` and now `eval` it, and `wc-guest.sh` hands it to its driver
as `${ROOTC@Q}`. A simulated driver ran `'$HOME/rootc'`, `env FOO=1 bash` and
`env BAR='a b' bash` as one argument each.

Re-run at 13:26 against the real guest: **72 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**
(`/tmp/wcrun/b12-guest-all-1.log`). That is the 64, plus the 8 checks that had
failed for harness reasons, minus `term`'s single FAIL, now that `term` is gone.

### 84.3 The window was in session 0, measured rather than inferred

§57 and commit 4531325 left this as "a window that EXISTS but never became
visible". The probe now prints where it is and, on failure, every candidate
window. The old leg was re-run once at 13:28 as a control (`wc-guest.sh damage`,
compositor and probe over ssh):

```
probe-scroll: session 0, station Service-0x0-153fe7b$, desktop Default, input desktop <unreachable>, screen 1024x768
probe-scroll: candidate hwnd …2e00be pid 5864 visible=0 WS_VISIBLE=1 iconic=0 … window 1024x768+26+23 client 1008x729 title="Mozilla Firefox"
```

`WS_VISIBLE` is set, and `IsWindowVisible` is false. The input desktop cannot
even be opened, so `SendInput` had nowhere to go even if the probe had tried. The
same leg through the scheduler (`wc-desktop.sh damage`, §13.3's route):

```
probe-scroll: session 1, station WinSta0, desktop Default, input desktop Default, screen 1280x800, desktop window …1000c visible=1 WS_VISIBLE=1
probe-scroll: target hwnd …e20752 pid 3812 visible=1 WS_VISIBLE=1 iconic=0 … client 1264x713 title="Troubleshooting Information "
probe-scroll: 60 of 60 notches towards the user accepted, 150 ms apart
```

**Not measured:** the desktop window's own visibility *in session 0*. I added
that line after the control run, and the session-0 explanation (the
non-interactive station's desktop window is not visible, so no top-level window
under it can be) is consistent with both outputs but has not been printed from
session 0. The control's verified commits (43, 0 stale) were an unscrolled
browser, as §57.1 feared.

The old leg also opened `about:blank` for every Firefox run, so even a wheel
that arrived would have scrolled an empty page. The new mode opens
`about:support`.

### 84.4 Scrolling found single-page corruption

The first session-1 run (13:30, arena `VirtualLock`ed, located by content sweep):

```
verified 535 commits (1956 state-only, unverifiable, 7 never reached the copy), 59 stale (worst 2 rows)
stale: … 1264x713 stride 5056 … -- 2 rows differ after copying extent …
```

The verifier compares immediately after the copy, in the same thread. A row
that differs there changed under the copy; it was not missed by it. Two rows is
the most a single 4096-byte page can touch at a 5056-byte stride, and the worst
was always 2, so **each stale commit is one page**. The photographs agree:
`docs/block12/block12-window-run1.png` and `block12-after-run1.png` show 2-px
seams of old content (y≈455 through the HEVC row, y≈170 through VP9, y≈580),
and the same run's screen capture shows them through the gaps around a console
window (84.8). The same proxy code reported 0 stale over 1030 commits on the
Wine file arena (§57.5), which points at the guest-RAM substrate rather than the
damage bookkeeping. To make the next occurrence self-explaining, the verifier now
prints, per stale row, whether the client's row moved since a pre-copy snapshot,
whether the destination kept what was written, and the arena page. **That
instrument has not yet seen a stale row**: the run that would have exercised it
was the control in 84.7.

### 84.5 `VirtualLock` keeps a page resident, not at one address

The next five attempts to run the leg failed at the locate, and each failure was
a measurement:

* content sweep: `3 page index(es) were claimed twice`, twice, then 51. That is
  one run's stamp found in two physical frames;
* the guest's own PFN query: `incomplete: 19 / 1 / 15 of 16384 pages missing`;
* once the query was complete (16384 frames in 674 ms), and the host's verify
  seconds later found `11260/16128` pages where the query had put them.

The stamps are written once, at startup, so a stamp in two frames means a page
was copied to a new frame after it was stamped. `wc-desktop.sh pinning`
measures this with nothing else running: one compositor, a 64 MiB arena, no
client, located by sweep three times 30 s apart in each session, plans compared
page by page. Results, in run order, are in `docs/block12/pinning.txt`:

| arena pinning | session-runs | with a duplicated stamp | pages that changed frame between two clean locates |
|---|---|---|---|
| stamp, then `VirtualLock` (the old order) | 2 | 2 (219→4→1 and 58→5→5 across the three locates) | n/a (no clean pair) |
| `VirtualLock`, then stamp | 13 | 7 (up to 324; once rising from 12 to 67 at +30 s) | 0 of 16384, every pair |
| `MEM_LARGE_PAGES` | 4 | **0** (12 of 12 locates clean) | **0 of 16384**, every pair |

Reordering helped and did not fix it. With the lock taken first, a stamp still
turned up in two frames, so **a locked page was relocated after it was
written**. Quiet stretches move nothing, which is also what `sf-probe --hold 30
--recheck` saw for a fresh `locked-va` window (16384/16384 unchanged). The
relocation comes in bursts. That fits 84.4: if a page moves mid-session, the host
keeps writing the old frame, the compositor shows the new one frozen, and
whatever Windows puts in the old frame overwrites the host's rows. I also tried
the PFN query (`--arena-frames`) as the trigger: it looked like the cause over
three runs and was refuted by the fourth (324 duplicates with it off).

Large pages are non-pageable and physically contiguous. The plans coalesce into
28–31 runs instead of ~1500. shared_vulkan's `sf-probe` already called them "the
chosen path". `alloc_locked_region` now tries `VirtualAlloc(MEM_LARGE_PAGES)`
first, after enabling `SeLockMemoryPrivilege` in its own token. If that fails it
falls back to lock-then-stamp, and the report line says which:
`pinning=large-pages|virtual-lock|mlock|none`. `--arena-small-pages` (or
`WC_ARENA_NO_LARGE_PAGES`) forces the fallback. **No system setting was changed
to get large pages.** The account on this guest already held the privilege
(`sf-probe --mode large-pages` allocated before any change of mine), and
`AdjustTokenPrivileges` only enables it in the running process.

### 84.6 The run

`wc-desktop.sh damage`, 14:21–14:24, compositor in session 1 via the scheduler,
arena `pinning=large-pages` located from the guest's own frame list (31 runs,
16128/16128 verified), proxy and Firefox on testhost, `--copy damage
--verify-damage`, `probe-scroll` in session 1 by pid:

```
2384 commits, 498 copies, 1290.91 MiB in 159.3 ms; 7 pools (2 released, 0 reclaimed, 0 republished, 3 resizes, 0 overflows, 0 refusals, 0 attaches deferred); 7 fds in, 2 out (2 from the arena); verified 498 commits (1879 state-only, unverifiable, 7 never reached the copy), 0 stale (worst 0 rows)
```

17 passed, 0 failed. The photographs are `docs/block12/block12-screen.png` (the
guest's desktop mid-scroll), `block12-window.png` and `block12-after.png` (the
window, by pid, through `PrintWindow`). A separate visual check of all six found
seams in every run-1 picture and none in these. The two screen captures have
their top 28 rows and left 37 columns greyed: that is a family member's desktop,
and the strips held desktop labels and a document title. Firefox starts at
(26,23) and nothing of it is lost but its border.

One run each way: 59/535 stale on `VirtualLock`, 0/498 on large pages. That is
evidence and not yet a statistic.

### 84.7 Incident: the guest hard-hung during the `VirtualLock` control run

To close 84.4 at commit level I started one control run of the same leg with
`--arena-small-pages` (16384 × 4 KiB, `VirtualLock` then stamp) and
`--arena-frames`. Timeline (CEST):

* 14:15–14:21 — six large-page arenas allocated and freed (the `pinning` runs),
  then the 14:21–14:24 run above. All of these completed normally.
* 14:25:53 — the control run starts: compositor pid 4644 as a session-1 task,
  PFN query 834 ms, locate clean, Firefox maps its window.
* 14:27:02 — the harness's last log line. Its next ssh to the guest, which would
  have registered `probe-scroll` as a task, never returned.
* ~14:31 — the coordinator found the guest unresponsive: all 12 vCPUs at 99% in
  QEMU, one kernel loop on every CPU, CPU 9 parked at a fixed RIP, no disk I/O,
  no ARP or ssh on either address, no guest-agent answer, and an injected NMI
  ignored. (The RIP values were taken by the coordinator and are not reproduced
  here.)
* 14:36 — my loop stopped locally; nothing on the guest or VM touched.
* 14:37 — the coordinator reset the guest with QMP `system_reset`. It came back
  healthy, with nobody logged in.

What is measured is the coincidence: the hang began during the one run that put
a `VirtualLock`ed arena under the host's writes *after* this section had shown
such pages relocating. What is **not** measured is the mechanism. The hypothesis
it suggests is serious enough to state: if a locked page relocates mid-session,
the host keeps writing Firefox's pixels into a frame that Windows has since
given to someone else, possibly the kernel, and that is a host writing into the
guest's memory. It is not established: a `VirtualLock`ed arena with the PFN query
had been allocated ten times before without a hang, and the one earlier run that
had the host writing pixels into a `VirtualLock`ed arena for minutes (84.4,
without the query) corrupted rows and did not hang. Standing rule from the coordinator since
then: no `--arena-frames` PFN scans and no small-page `VirtualLock` arenas on
the real guest until the hang is understood.

### 84.8 What else changed in the harnesses

* `wc-guest.sh damage` hands over to `wc-desktop.sh damage` and folds its counts
  in. The driver's ssh-session scroll path is gone. The verdict is
  `wc_damage_verdict` (`scripts/wc-damage-verdict.sh`), shared by both.
* `wc-desktop.sh`: `do_window`'s bring-up and host side are now `desk_up` and
  `hostside_start`, shared with `damage`. `locate_arena` wraps
  `wc_locate_arena`, so the frame list is used first, as in wc-icon/wc-taskbar.
  Captures run from a hidden PowerShell (`int_quiet`), because run 1's
  `cmd.exe /c` console covered Firefox at the very spot where the probe parks
  the cursor. `deploy` kills everything running from its own directory (a stale
  `probe-relay.exe` blocked one `scp`). New mode: `pinning`. `WC_COMP_EXTRA`
  passes extra compositor flags.
* `wc_locate_arena` took every `N pages` on the report line, and a `frames=none
  (… 19 of 16384 pages missing …)` tail made `--pages` two lines (`16384:
  command not found`). Fixed there and in two copies of the same grep.
* `probe-scroll`: `--pid`, its own session/station/desktop and the desktop
  window's visibility, and one line per candidate window when none qualifies.

### 84.9 The gates

Local gates on the merged tree (master fe24480 merged in), run with
`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2` because the shared slice was at 9.5 of 10 GB and the first
attempt was starved:

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` | **92 binaries, 2735 passed, 0 failed**, 8 ignored, including `every_design_document_citation_resolves` (it failed while this section did not exist yet, on this branch's own `§82` citations, which became `§84`) |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` | exit 0; 32 warnings, none at a line this branch wrote |
| `cargo check --workspace --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` | exit 0 |
| `scripts/wc-pool.sh`, `scripts/wc-keymap.sh` | `wc-pool: OK`, `wc-keymap: OK`, both legs |
| `scripts/wc-desktop.sh psgate` | **SKIP**: no `pwsh` on this machine, so the generated PowerShell (now including `int_quiet`'s) is unchecked |
| `bash -n` on the twelve scripts touched | clean |

On the real guest, each run once:

| run | result |
|---|---|
| `wc-guest.sh all` (13:26, before the damage hand-over) | **72 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (was 64/9) |
| `wc-guest.sh damage`, old ssh-session leg, as a control (13:28) | window `WS_VISIBLE=1`, `IsWindowVisible=0`, session 0; no scroll; 43 verified, 0 stale |
| `wc-desktop.sh damage`, `VirtualLock` arena (13:30) | visible, 60/60 notches; **59 of 535 stale, worst 2 rows** |
| `wc-desktop.sh damage`, six more attempts (13:36–13:56) | five stopped at the locate (84.5), one at deploy (a stale `probe-relay.exe`, 84.8) |
| `wc-desktop.sh pinning` (13:47–14:21) | the table in 84.5 |
| **`wc-desktop.sh damage`, large pages (14:21)** | **17 passed, 0 failed: visible, 60/60 notches, 0 of 498 stale** |
| control, `--arena-small-pages` (14:25) | guest hard-hung, 84.7 |

### 84.10 What is not proven

1. **Why the guest hung.** 84.7's hypothesis is a hypothesis. Until it is
   settled, the `VirtualLock` fallback should be read as possibly unsafe, not
   just possibly stale: it is what runs on any account without
   `SeLockMemoryPrivilege`, and a default Windows account does not have it.
   Making the guest-RAM arena *refuse* without large pages (or use AWE pages) is
   the conservative change. It is not made here, because it changes what every
   harness can run. *Made in §85.2: large pages or a refusal, and `VirtualLock`
   only under `--arena-small-pages-may-corrupt-guest-memory`.*
2. **The relocation's cause inside Windows.** Measured: it happens, in bursts,
   to locked 4 KiB pages, and not to large pages. Not measured: what triggers it
   (memory compaction for some contiguous allocation is the usual suspect; the
   six large-page allocations just before the hang are themselves a candidate).
3. **Large pages over time.** 12 locates over about 6 minutes and one 3-minute
   damage run. A long session, and a guest under memory pressure where a 2 MiB
   allocation can fail, are not covered. On failure the fallback is the path
   item 1 is about.
4. **`wc-desktop.sh window` and `fps`** were refactored (`desk_up`,
   `locate_arena`, `int_quiet` not used by them) and not re-run. `damage` runs
   the shared parts.
5. **`wc-guest.sh all` after the last harness commits.** The 72/0 run predates
   the damage hand-over and the driver's scroll-path removal. Neither is on
   `all`'s path except as deleted code (the driver no longer takes a scroll
   prefix it was already passed empty), but it has not been re-run; the guest
   was reset and nobody is logged in.
6. **The stale-row instrument** (84.4) has not yet printed a stale row.

## 85. Firefox polish: large pages or nothing, a session that ends, and popups that behave

Written 2026-10-15, on branch `firefox-polish`. Seven items, all compositor-side
and all checked on this workstation: the Linux build, `wc-compositor.exe` under
Wine 11.14 on Xvfb, WLCS, a local NixOS VM and a local Firefox 157. **Nothing
here ran on the Windows guest.** 85.10 lists what needs it, with the commands.

### 85.1 Status in one paragraph

A guest-RAM arena now **refuses to start without large pages**. The
`VirtualLock` path that §84.5 measured moving and §84.7 ran into a hang is
reachable only under `--arena-small-pages-may-corrupt-guest-memory`. Popup grabs
are a stack: they take the keyboard and close in one click. The conformance
stand-in now runs interactive moves and resizes itself, two subsurface orderings
are fixed in `vendor/smithay`, and a reference run against Mir settles §74.4.
**WLCS headless goes from 416 passed / 50 failed to 428 / 38, and the debts
from 20 to 10.** A launcher session now ends when its last window has been gone
for `linger-secs`, and it never ends while a client is still connected. That
second rule exists because of the one finding in this section that bears on
the user's "crashed Firefox" reports: **Firefox records a lost display
connection as a crash** (85.3). No compositor fault reproduced, in 10 minutes
of Wine stress or under gdb on Linux. The first-frame stall is not on this
side (85.8).

### 85.2 The arena: large pages or nothing

`alloc_locked_region` used to try `MEM_LARGE_PAGES` and fall back to
`VirtualLock` silently. It now takes a policy:

* **`LargePagesOrRefuse`**, the default. On Windows this is
  `VirtualAlloc(MEM_LARGE_PAGES)`. On Linux it is `mmap(MAP_HUGETLB)` from
  `vm.nr_hugepages`, and its report is `pinning=hugetlb`. If neither is
  available, `attach_guest_ram` returns `Unsupported` with the platform's
  reason, why small pages are not a fallback, and the ways out:
  `--arena-ivshmem`, `SeLockMemoryPrivilege` via
  `scripts/win-account-right.ps1`, or the flag below.
* **`SmallPagesMayCorruptGuestMemory`**, the diagnostic. The compositor flag
  `--arena-small-pages-may-corrupt-guest-memory`, or
  `WC_ARENA_SMALL_PAGES_MAY_CORRUPT_GUEST_MEMORY` for other processes, selects
  it. It always takes `VirtualLock`/`mlock`, as `--arena-small-pages` did.
  §84's `--arena-small-pages` and `WC_ARENA_NO_LARGE_PAGES` are refused by name,
  with the new name in the message. A harness that still passed them would
  otherwise quietly get large pages and believe it had run the control.

Linux applies the same rule because `mlock` has the same flaw: compaction
migrates mlocked pages unless `vm.compact_unevictable_allowed` is 0. Hugetlb
pages are not moved by kcompactd, but an explicit migration can still move them
(offlining, a contiguous allocation). **No Linux guest was measured for
relocation**, so `hugetlb` is the stronger of the two Linux pinnings and not a
measured equivalent of Windows' large pages.

**A latent fallback went with it.** The large-page path required the requested
length to be a multiple of `GetLargePageMinimum()`. A growth request is a pool's
length and almost never is one, so before this **every grown region took
`VirtualLock`** while the startup region reported `large-pages`. The large-page
path now rounds up, and the caller is told the length it got.
`create_outbound`'s own region makes the whole rounded region its window, so
every stamped page is one the host is told about.

Measured:

| run | result |
|---|---|
| `wc-compositor.exe --arena-guest-ram 0:64MiB` under Wine (no privilege) | exit 2: `refusing a guest-RAM arena without large pages: this account does not hold SeLockMemoryPrivilege, which large pages need. …` |
| the same with `--arena-small-pages-may-corrupt-guest-memory` | starts, `pinning=none` (Wine's `VirtualLock` fails) |
| the same with `--arena-small-pages` | exit 2, the retirement message |
| `scripts/wc-vm-damage.sh linux` (Linux compositor in the local NixOS VM, which now reserves `nr_hugepages`) | `pinning=hugetlb`, frame list 16384 frames, **verify 16128/16128**; 13 passed, 2 failed, which is §71.6's score and §71.5's wire |

That harness also had a bug of its own. Outside its heredoc the host relay's
line ended in `\\`, a literal backslash, so `socat` got three addresses and
exited. It is fixed. `wc-release-vm.sh` reserves hugetlb pages the same way and
was not run. `wc-desktop.sh pinning` now measures large pages only, and the
`VirtualLock` rows need `WC_PIN_COMP_EXTRA=--arena-small-pages-may-corrupt-guest-memory`,
which the standing rule forbids on the real guest. No other harness passed the
old flag. The real-guest harnesses (`wc-guest.sh`, `wc-desktop.sh`,
`wc-icon.sh`, `wc-taskbar.sh`, `wc-titlebar.sh`) all get large pages on this
guest, whose account holds the privilege (§84.5). **None of them was re-run.**

Unit tests: the default policy either produces `large-pages`/`hugetlb` with a
length rounded up to 2 MiB, or fails `Unsupported` with the flag and
`--arena-ivshmem` in the message and nothing registered. The diagnostic policy
reports its pinning by name. The policy resolution is tested, including the
retired variable. The compositor refuses the retired flag and accepts the new
one. Four `wc-handle` integration tests used to *skip* when the commit failed
(`if … is_err() { return }`). They now ask for small pages by name, so they run
rather than skip silently.

### 85.3 Crashes: nothing reproduced, and what "crashed Firefox" most likely is

**Stress.** `wc-compositor.exe` under Wine and `wc-proxy` ran a page that opens
and closes up to ten windows every 150 ms, resizes and moves each of them,
retitles itself every 50 ms in three scripts (`é中😀`), and animates a canvas.
Over it, `xdotool` drove random moves, left and right clicks, Escape, Alt,
drags, double clicks, `ctrl+t`, `ctrl+Tab` and an occasional `ctrl+w`. Over
10 minutes and 2351 input actions there were **208 toplevels and 162 popups,
the compositor alive at the end, and Firefox alive at the end**. Shorter runs
before it (40 s, 5 min, 60 s) also had no fault. The Linux compositor (headless platform) also ran under `gdb`, with Firefox
connected to it directly and the same window storm, ten windows every 150 ms
with no input. The run made in isolation lasted the full 600 s: **1471
toplevels**, 20144 retitles, no signal and no panic. Firefox ended at its own
`timeout` (124). An earlier run of the same script, made while other Wine runs
were going on beside it, ended 76 s early. Firefox exited with 11 and "Error
reading events from display: Broken pipe", the compositor's log stopped
without a line, and `gdb` printed no signal. **That one is not explained.** It
is consistent with something outside killing the debugger, and it did not
recur on its own.

**What did reproduce is a crash *report*, and it is Firefox's.** With Firefox
running through the proxy, killing the compositor or killing the proxy leaves
Firefox gone and a crash event in its profile's `crashes/events`. Each of the
two runs left one event, with the same reason:

```
"MozCrashReason":"() Error reading events from display: Broken pipe Proxy: WP:E WP:RT WP:CA WP:CR WP:CPCA WP:CPCF "
```

GTK's display error goes through `MOZ_CRASH`. Every way a session can end under
a running browser therefore files a crash: a deploy that kills `sv-guest.exe`, a
harness `pkill`, the compositor's 12-hour `--timeout` (§28.9 item 1), and a
compositor that faults. §28.9 item 11 found "Exiting due to channel error" in
the logs and rightly said it proves nothing. The crash event is the artefact
that would appear in Firefox's own UI as "Firefox closed unexpectedly". That
this is what the user saw is **a hypothesis**, not measured on the guest; the
guest command is in 85.10. What changed: a session no longer ends under a
connected client (85.7).

**Not reproduced:** §28.6's six start-up segfaults (`0xc0000005` at
`wc-compositor.exe+0x123100`, before the first `println!`, on the real guest).
A fault before `main` prints is not something a Wine or Linux run reaches, and
that binary is gone. It stays §28.9 item 5.

### 85.4 Popups and menus (§78.4, §78.5)

**Grabs are a stack** (`State::popup_grabs`, outermost first).

* A click that ends outside every grab dismisses **all** of them, innermost
  first, in one go. A click inside grab *i*, or inside a popup that hangs off
  it, dismisses only the grabs above *i*. Stage 13 dismissed one level per click
  and relied on the client destroying the popup to expose the next. A client
  that does not destroy on `popup_done` left the outer menu up, and WLCS's
  client does not.
* The innermost grab that hangs off the focused toplevel **takes the
  keyboard**. `keyboard_focus` stays what Windows says, the `HWND` with
  `WM_SETFOCUS`. The surface smithay is told is `keyboard_target()`, and it
  goes back to the next grab or to the toplevel when the grab ends.
* A new toplevel ends every grab, and so does the grab's toplevel losing
  activation. On Windows that is a click in another application, which this
  compositor never sees as a click, so a menu stayed open over whatever the
  user had switched to.
* **Reactive popups** (`set_reactive`) are reconstrained every turn against
  their parent's bounds. A change gets a bare `configure`, with no
  `repositioned`, and a `MovePopup`.
* **On Win32 every owned popup now follows its owner.** An owned `WS_POPUP`
  does not move with its owner, and `xdg_popup` is positioned relative to its
  parent, so a menu open while its window moved stayed where the window had
  been. `WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGED` now puts each mapped popup back at its offset.
  This is compiled and checked for Windows; it was not run on Windows, and
  Wine's virtual desktop gave no move to test it with.

**Moves and resizes hand the pointer over.** `xdg_toplevel.move`/`resize` now
sends the client `leave`, unsets smithay's click grab and empties its pressed
set (`hand_pointer_to_platform`). `SC_MOVE`'s modal loop eats the
`WM_LBUTTONUP`, so the implicit click grab used to outlive the move. Every
motion over another surface of ours then went to the dragged window until the
next click. That follows from smithay's `ClickGrab` and was not observed on the
guest. `win32.rs` also resets its capture count, for the same reason. The
stand-in (`control.rs`) now runs the gesture the way the modal loop does. It
starts only while a button is held, moves or resizes with the pointer, sends
nothing to the client meanwhile, eats the release and re-enters wherever the
pointer is. §64's four "headless has no window manager" excuses are gone; all
four pass.

**`vendor/smithay`, two fixes.** A zero-size anchor rectangle is legal: the
protocol raises `invalid_input` for a *negative* one. A subsurface position is
now the parent's *committed* state. §68 kept one stage where the protocol has
two, so a sync middle level moved its children whenever the grandparent
committed, whether it had committed itself or not.

**Reference run.** Mir 2.29 (nixpkgs `mir`, `miral_wlcs_integration.so`,
under the wlcs 1.8.1 built against the same nixpkgs) on the five remaining
subsurface failures:

| test | Mir 2.29 | here |
|---|---|---|
| `subsurface_with_sync_parent_does_not_move_when_only_grandparent_committed` | pass | **pass** (was fail) |
| `subsurface_does_not_move_when_grandparent_commit_is_before_sync_parent_commit` | pass | **pass** (was fail) |
| `place_above_simple` | fail, first assertion | fail, second assertion |
| `place_below_simple` | fail, first assertion | fail, second assertion |
| `subsurface_extends_parent_input_region` | fail, "bad optional access" | fail, the same |

Mir also lists all three failures in its `expected_wlcs_failures.list`. The two
restacking tests are now in `wc-wlcs.sh`'s expected table, headless only, with
that reason. Here the first assertion (the restack took effect) passes and the
second asserts that the restacked subsurface is not on top either.
`subsurface_extends_parent_input_region` stays a debt. Failing it the same way
as Mir is not an explanation.

**WLCS headless:**

| passed / failed / skipped | 416 / 50 / 759 | **428 / 38 / 759** |
| expected on this leg | 30 | 28 (26 §45.4, 2 above) |

**Firefox's menus under Wine.** A right-click menu, Down twice, Escape, then

Measured from the compositor's log: **Firefox called `xdg_popup.grab` zero

so the grab work above changes nothing for Firefox's own menus. It matters for
GTK clients and for the protocol. One click on the page destroyed both levels
of View ▸ Sidebar (windows 4 and 3, in that order). A visual check by a separate agent

drawn opaque. On the guest `UpdateLayeredWindow` composites that margin away.
Under Wine's virtual desktop on Xvfb it does not, and the cause was not
pinned down. §18.5's guest photograph is the evidence that the guest is right.

### 85.5 Title and taskbar with Firefox

Under a Wine **shell** desktop (`explorer /desktop=shell,…`, which draws a

what `SetWindowTextW` sets. **Alt-Tab itself was not photographed.**

The icon: the compositor logged `icon <- 3 image(s) published for "firefox"`
and `WM_SETICON` big 32×32 and small 16×16. The Wine taskbar button showed

So Wine cannot answer this question. The taskbar photograph with Firefox is a

(IDC_SIZENS)` ×9, `grab (IDC_HAND)` ×6, `crosshair` ×5, `help` ×3, `wait` ×1,

### 85.7 Session lifecycle, and two applications on one arena

`wc-compositor --exit-when-empty <secs>` (`EmptyWatch`) ends the process once
three things hold:

1. it has had a toplevel;
2. it has had none for `secs`, with no client connecting in that time;
3. **no client is connected now.**

A connecting client restarts the wait, because a click into an empty session
starts an application that connects long before its first window. Under
`--exit-when-empty` the `--timeout` deadline also waits for the clients to
go, and says so once. Both follow from 85.3: ending a session under a
connected Firefox is a crash report.

`wc-launch` passes `[session] linger-secs` (default 60), and `supervise()`
already tears the relay, the tunnel and the host side down when the compositor
exits. So the session stops holding the arena (§28.9 item 9). A click that
joins a session as it ends now waits for the old owner to let go and starts a
new one, once. That launcher path is compiled for Windows and is clippy-clean.
It was not run, because it runs only on the guest.

Measured under Wine with Firefox and `--exit-when-empty 10`: `ctrl+q`, six
disconnects, the toplevel destroyed, and the compositor gone **11.7 s** after
the keystroke with the new line.

**Two applications, one session, one arena** (Wine; the file-arena fixture,
`SV_ALLOW_FILE_ARENA=1`, as `wc-firefox.sh wine-arena` uses it): Firefox, then
`weston-terminal`, both through one `wc-proxy --transport arena` into one
compositor.

* Two toplevels, with app ids `firefox` and
  `org.freedesktop.weston.wayland-terminal`.
* Five connections joined arena 0, with 0 overflows and 0 refusals.
* Closing the terminal left the session up.
* Closing Firefox ended it after 9 s, with linger 8.

**On screen, the second toplevel is solid black**
(`docs/firefox-polish/two-apps-second-window-black.png`; the frame the
compositor actually received is `two-apps-terminal-frame-dump.png`), whichever application it
belongs to: Firefox's own second window from `window.open` is black too. The
compositor received the right pixels (its frame dump shows the terminal's
prompt). Instrumented, `WM_PAINT` arrived and `SetDIBitsToDevice` returned 441
of 441 lines from a non-black buffer. **Master's `wc-compositor.exe` (dff9e3b)
does the same**, so it is not a regression. The Wine-drawn caption of that
window is black as well. That points below the blit, at Wine's virtual desktop.
The cause was not found. On the guest §32 photographed two applications' windows
side by side, drawn. A guest re-run with Firefox as one of the two is in 85.10.

### 85.8 First frame

Under Wine, from `exec firefox` to the compositor's first log line of each kind,
three runs:

| | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| first client connected | 0.06 s | 0.05 s | 0.06 s |
| `xdg_toplevel` created | 1.09 s | 0.95 s | 0.96 s |
| window mapped (first frame) | 1.09 s | 1.00 s | 1.02 s |

So on the `wl_shm` path the compositor turns Firefox's first commit into a
window in the same second, and the whole start is about one second. The ~15 s
of §34/`docs/firefox-accel.md` is the **forwarded GPU present**: 216.9 ms per
`vkQueuePresentKHR`, which is eleven 20 ms doorbell slices. That is
`sv_transport::park`, not the compositor, and it belongs to the accel work.
This run did not re-measure it on the guest.

## 86. Deploying to the real guest: sound, a GPU path with no root in Firefox, a driver fault, and a VM that stopped

Written 2026-10-15, on branch `deploy-guest`, on master 40935af with d9b3a27
(§85) merged in. The brief was integration on the real machines: audio, the
accelerated path, hardware decode and the end-to-end launcher run. What is in
this section, in order: what was deployed (86.2), the accelerated path as far as
it got (86.3), the driver fault that stopped it (86.4), the incident that fault
led to and the rule that came out of it (86.5), sound (86.6), the GPU and decode
wiring for the launcher, committed and **not** enabled (86.7), the gates (86.8)
and what remains (86.9). Nobody was logged in to the guest at any point, so
every guest run here was in session 0.

### 86.1 Status in one paragraph

**Sound works end to end on the real guest.** A Firefox started by
`wc-launch.exe` played a WebAudio tone for 63.4 s through a per-session
PulseAudio on testhost, over the launcher's own tunnel, into waveOut in the
guest: 63.4 s played, all of it non-silent, 0 chunks dropped, 2 underruns. A
session without a server gives Firefox `media.cubeb.force_null_context` and says
so on both machines, so the stall of docs/design.md §0.28.9 cannot happen on the
launcher's path any more. **The accelerated path reached the guest's Intel GPU
and stopped at a driver fault**: eglinfo on the Wayland platform names
`zink Vulkan 1.4(Intel(R) UHD Graphics …) Mesa 26.2.4`, Firefox's renderer
faults the GPU side inside Intel's `igvk64.dll` on its first pipeline layout,
and the layout that does it is isolated (86.4). **The isolation run was followed
within seconds by QEMU stopping the VM** (86.5); the coordinator reset it. GPU
work on the guest is suspended until the fault is fixed on our side, which
another branch (`intel-layout-fix`) owns. The launcher's GPU and decode wiring
is committed and off.

### 86.2 What was deployed, and where

| where | what |
|---|---|
| testhost store | Firefox 157.0.1 `/nix/store/a6d0xgdw14rjpw84frvyxcqhyf8qmbwy-firefox-157.0.1` (nixpkgs#firefox, the build `mesa-kopper-wayland` was made against: both use `wayland-1.26.0` li1008…); `/nix/store/9nnjvvqxg5c71k18wv4iqqb9fxnd0fvy-mesa-kopper-wayland-26.2.4`; `mesa-demos-9.0.0` p2si5i…; `pulseaudio-17.0` xmgw0c…; `vulkan-tools-lunarg-1.4.357.0` rrbwd0…; the readback Firefox `/nix/store/aqgy9hl76pgiwnjbdi106wmi4gzlm6zj-firefox-readback-157.0.1` (without the 86.7 marker; the marked rebuild, rk9rz1…, is on the workstation only) |
| testhost `~/wc-launch-ivs` | `wc-session` (this branch), `bin/wc-proxy`, `bin/wc-arena-host`, `bin/pulse` → pulseaudio-17.0 as an indirect GC root. **No** `gpu.env`, no `sv-hostd`, no ICD |
| testhost `/tmp/svff-int` | the harness's release `sv-hostd`, `wc-proxy`, `libsv_icd.so`, `sv_icd.json`, `video-probe`, and the logs and `apidump.txt` of 86.3–86.4 |
| guest `C:\Users\<guest-user>\wcivs` | `wc-launch.exe`, `sv-guest.exe` (compositor half only), `wc-desk.exe`, `probe-relay.exe`, `wc-launch.ini` with `audio = on`, `gpu-sessions = 0` |
| guest `C:\Users\<guest-user>\svffint` | release `sv-guest.exe` (both halves), `video-probe.exe`, `probe-relay.exe`. `layout-probe.exe` was **deleted** after 86.5 so that nobody runs it by accident |
| NixOS | unchanged: generation 50, 102f747 |

### 86.3 The accelerated path, on the guest's GPU

`scripts/sv-firefox-guest.sh` as the accel agent left it could not be run here:
its compositor used `--arena-guest-ram` with `--arena-frames`, the two things
§84.7's rule forbids on this guest, and its root was `~/rootc`, which is gone.
This branch changed it to the ivshmem arena (`--arena-ivshmem 0`, the header
checked in the file as `wc-session up` checks it), root through `sudokey` for
`sv-hostd` and nothing else, the proxy and Firefox as `sirati`, and an exit trap
that ends its own guest processes by path. Two code changes made the last part
possible and safer:

* **`sv-hostd qemu-serve --drop-to UID:GID`.** The locate needs QMP and
  `/proc/<qemu-pid>/fd`, both root's. After it, `sv-hostd` drops every id,
  clears supplementary groups, makes itself dumpable again, refuses to go on if
  `setuid(0)` still works, and hands out `/proc/<its own pid>/fd/<n>` instead of
  QEMU's descriptor. Measured on testhost: `now uid 1000 gid 100; serving
  /proc/198066/fd/4`, `icd.sock` owned by `sirati`, and Firefox and eglinfo
  ran as `sirati`. Until now the harness ran Firefox as root.
* **The GPU side refuses `VirtualLock` arenas.** `sv-gpu-server guest` used
  large pages and fell back to locked 4 KiB pages; §84.5 measured such pages
  moving frame under the host's writes, and the host writes this arena on every
  command. The fallback now needs `--allow-small-pages` or
  `SV_ALLOW_SMALL_PAGES=1`. Every GPU side here reported `large-pages window:
  80 MiB of guest RAM`.

Measured, session 0:

| run | result |
|---|---|
| locate of one 80 MiB GPU arena (×14) | 2.19–2.25 s each, 7–27 runs, `all 20480 pages carry their own index` |
| `probe`, stock Mesa 26.2.0 (control) | Wayland platform: `zink Vulkan 1.4(Intel(R) UHD Graphics (Driver Unknown))`, Mesa 26.2.0 |
| `probe`, `mesa-kopper-wayland` 26.2.4 | Wayland platform: `zink Vulkan 1.4(Intel(R) UHD Graphics (Driver Unknown))`, **Mesa 26.2.4** |
| ICD ring waits in a probe, no doorbell | 1657 waits, mean 6.49 ms, `[<10us=444 <100us=532 <1ms=28 <10ms=258 <100ms=395]`; 1356, mean 7.89 ms in the other |
| `zink`, Firefox 157, `SV_DEBUG=1` | GPU side 1 **faulted**; Firefox `DeviceLost`, `vkCreatePipelineLayout failed (VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST)`; window 1×1 |
| the same with `SV_TRACE=pre` on the GPU sides | no fault; every `eglChooseConfig` for WebRender failed and Firefox fell back to software WebRender (`InitDeviceTask is slow: 14280`) |
| the same with `ZINK_DEBUG=nopc` | faulted, in the same place |

So the stock control *also* reaches Zink here, unlike on the workstation
(docs/design.md §0.28.1). Why the harness's Mesa 26.2.0 behaves differently from the
workstation's stock 26.2.4 was not investigated. The present's
`fence … ms` was **not** measured: no Firefox frame was presented on the GPU.
The doorbell port (§36.16) was not hot-added; the ring-wait histogram above is
what the 20 ms slice costs without it, and the many waits in the
`<100ms` bucket say a usable frame rate will need it.

### 86.4 The fault: Intel's driver, `vkCreatePipelineLayout`, one layout

The GPU side died as a bare `Segmentation fault` from MSYS. It now carries
`sv_gpu_server::fault`: each ring stores its in-flight opcode and seqno in one
relaxed atomic before dispatch and marks it returned after, and on Windows an
unhandled-exception filter prints the exception, its module and every ring's
last command. Three runs, the same answer each time:

```
[gpu] FAULT: exception 0xc0000005 at 0x7ff8bccab8d3 in C:\WINDOWS\System32\DriverStore\FileRepository\iigd_dch.inf_amd64_a8d32ac2abbe057a\igvk64.dll+0xdb8d3
[gpu] FAULT: read of 0x8
  ring 2: seqno 195 vkCreatePipelineLayout (IN THE DRIVER)
```

The LunarG api_dump layer between Zink and the ICD on the host gave the
arguments: `flags 0`, three set layouts — `0xc`, `PUSH_DESCRIPTOR`, five
`UNIFORM_BUFFER` bindings, one per graphics stage, with a
`VkDescriptorSetLayoutBindingFlagsCreateInfo` whose five flags are all zero;
`0xe`, Zink's empty dummy layout; `0x6f`, one `UNIFORM_TEXEL_BUFFER` for the
fragment stage — and a push-constant range `ALL_GRAPHICS 0..52`. None is null
and the forwarder translated all three to driver handles, so `read of 0x8` is
not a null handle of ours. Zink's separable-shader path, which does pass null
set layouts, was ruled out by `nopc` above.

`vk-probe`'s `layout-probe` made that layout and variations directly on the
driver, with no forwarder, one child process per variation:

| variation | result |
|---|---|
| the layout above, exactly | **0xc0000005** |
| the same without the binding-flags pNext | ok |
| push set + empty set | **0xc0000005** |
| push set + texel set | **0xc0000005** |
| empty set + texel set | ok |
| an ordinary (not push) UBO set + empty + texel | ok |
| push set alone, empty set alone | not run (86.5) |

So the fault needs a `PUSH_DESCRIPTOR` set layout that carries a binding-flags
pNext, in a pipeline layout with at least one set after it. Dropping an
all-zero binding-flags struct from push-descriptor layouts on this driver
avoids it in this probe; that fix, and proving it, belong to
`intel-layout-fix`. Driver version: the guest's Intel UHD driver, igvk64.dll
from `iigd_dch.inf_amd64_a8d32ac2abbe057a`.

### 86.5 Incident: QEMU stopped the VM after the driver faulted three times

`layout-probe.exe` ran in the guest at about 17:06–17:07 CEST. It printed the
first six rows of 86.4 — three of them a fault in `igvk64.dll` within a few
seconds — and nothing more. The watchdog saw ssh and ping fail at 17:07:41.
Read-only diagnosis, nothing reset or resumed by this branch:

* `query-status`: `{"status": "internal-error", "running": false}`;
* QEMU's journal at 17:07:16: `error: kvm run failed Bad address`, then the
  vCPU's registers: `CPL=0`, `RIP=fffff8052cee1a63`, the instruction
  `41 8b 0f` (`mov ecx,[r15]`) with `r15 = fffff971a9730044`, inside a loop
  whose registers hold a timeout computation (`rcx = 10,000,000`);
* every vCPU thread asleep, load 0.08, QEMU's I/O counters unchanged over 5 s.
  That is not §84.7's hang, where all twelve vCPUs spun at 99%.

`KVM_RUN` returned `EFAULT` while the guest kernel was reading what has the
shape of a device register in a polling loop. The likely mechanism is the
passed-through iGPU being reset after the user-mode faults, with VFIO revoking
the BAR mapping under that read. **That is an inference from the shape of the
registers, not a measurement.** The earlier Firefox runs faulted the same driver
once each and the VM carried on; this run faulted it three times in a few
seconds. The coordinator recovered the guest with QMP `system_reset` and `cont`
at 17:12; the Intel GPU and the ivshmem device both reported OK afterwards.

**The rule, from the coordinator, and this section is where it is written down:
bisecting a driver crash never runs on the guest.** A user-mode fault in the
Intel driver on this VM can take the VM down, which a fault in a process on a
machine with its own GPU does not. Isolate on a local driver, reason from the
api_dump, or fix the forwarder so the driver never sees the input; the guest
gets the fixed build once it is proven elsewhere. `layout-probe` carries that
warning at the top of its source.

### 86.6 Sound

**Where the speakers are.** testhost's QEMU has `-audiodev
alsa,…,out.dev=hw:0,0` behind an emulated `intel-hda`, so the guest owns the
card exclusively; `testhost-mixer-unity.service` pins the host mixer to 100%
for it; there is no PipeWire or Pulse for `sirati` and `/dev/snd` is group
`audio`. Routing Firefox into the host's audio stack would mean a server that
shares `hw:0,0` with QEMU, which is a change to `windows-vm.service` and a VM
restart. So the route is into the guest: what Firefox plays is played by
Windows.

**The route.**

1. `wc-session proxy` also starts `wc-launch-audio-<ID>`, a user unit running
   `pulseaudio -n` with a null sink `wc` (s16le, 48 kHz, stereo), its native
   socket at `$D/xdg/pulse/native` — libpulse's default under the
   `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` Firefox is already given, so Firefox needs no setting —
   and `module-simple-protocol-unix` serving the sink's monitor as raw PCM on
   `$D/audio.sock`. `down` stops the unit. The package is `$BIN/pulse`, a GC
   root that `wc-launch.sh deploy` makes from `WC_LAUNCH_PULSE`.
2. The launcher's tunnel gains `-L 127.0.0.1:<audio-port>:$D/audio.sock`
   (`audio-port` defaults to `port + 1`).
3. `wc-launch.exe` connects there and plays the stream with waveOut through a
   queue of 8 × 20 ms buffers. A chunk that finds all eight queued is dropped,
   so the delay never grows past 160 ms; a device that runs dry is an underrun.
   Both are counted. `audio-volume` sets waveOut's volume for this stream.
4. With no server (`audio.state` says why), `run` writes
   `media.cubeb.force_null_context` into `user.js` and prints `NO AUDIO … Firefox
   gets media.cubeb.force_null_context` to the app log and to the launcher, which
   logs it. A null sink consumes in real time whether or not anyone is
   connected, so a Firefox with a server never waits on it either.

**The first route did not work, and why it was abandoned rather than fixed.**
Version one ran a `wc-session audio ID` verb (`parec` to stdout) over its own
ssh exec and read ssh.exe's stdout from a pipe `wc-launch.exe` created. The
player received nothing: `parec` wrote 2.25 MB and blocked, while ssh.exe on
the guest wrote nothing into the pipe. The same command through an MSYS pipe
streamed 1.52 MB in 8 s, with or without `-n`. So Win32 ssh.exe and that pipe do
not get on; the cause was not found. The tunnel already belongs to the session,
so the socket costs nothing new, and the verb is kept for a person diagnosing.

**Measured, session 0 on the real guest, Firefox 157 in software WebRender**
(no GPU environment), a page playing a 440 Hz WebAudio tone at gain 0.05 and
putting its `AudioContext` state and clock in the title:

| | |
|---|---|
| `waveOutOpen` in session 0 | succeeded (`WAVE_MAPPER`) |
| player, at the end of the session | **63.4 s played, 63.4 s of it not silent, 0 chunks dropped, 2 underruns** |
| Firefox's clock, from the compositor's title log | `tone running t=62.2` when the player said 60.0 s |
| Pulse on the host | sink input `application.name = "Firefox"`, float32le 2ch 48 kHz, `Corked: no`, buffer latency 31.25 ms, sink latency 13.5 ms; source output `protocol-simple.c` s16le 2ch 48 kHz; sink `wc` RUNNING |
| teardown | both user units stopped, no `pulseaudio`, `parec`, `wc-proxy` or Firefox left |
| the fallback, by hand on the workstation | no `audio.state`: `run ok … audio=none`, the `NO AUDIO` line in both places, `force_null_context` appended; with one: nothing appended |

The guest played the tone at 5% waveOut volume on the laptop's speakers, with
nobody logged in, for about two minutes in total. Two things this run found
that are not sound: Firefox stopped at **"Open Firefox in Troubleshoot Mode?"**
on the first try, because earlier launcher sessions had ended under it and
counted as startup crashes (`toolkit.startup.max_resumed_crashes=-1` was set for
the test, through `WC_LAUNCH_EXTRA_PREFS`, not in the product); and a run
directory's `xdg/` survives `down`, recreated after `rm -rf` by the Firefox
that `down` does not stop. That predates this section (a §83 directory had the
same) and was cleaned up by hand.

**Not measured:** what anybody heard (session 0, nobody there); the delay from
the null sink to the speakers, and so how far the picture leads the sound —
up to the 160 ms queue plus the tunnel, with Firefox's audio clock running on
the host's null sink and knowing none of it; drift over an hour; session 1,
where the user's own audio device and volume apply; and `<video>` with sound.

### 86.7 The GPU and decode wiring for the launcher: committed, not enabled

What the launcher needs to give Firefox the guest's GPU, and none of it is
switched on: testhost has no `gpu.env`, no `sv-hostd` in `~/wc-launch-ivs`,
no broker running, and the deployed ini says `gpu-sessions = 0`.

* **Guest.** `[session] gpu-sessions = N` (0..=8, default 0), `gpu-port`
  (default `port + 10`), `gpu-arena-mib` (default 64). After the proxy,
  `wc-launch.exe` starts N `sv-guest.exe gpu guest --port … --arena … --idle
  <session-secs>` (large pages or a refusal), waits for each to publish, and
  calls `wc-session gpu ID N`. The tunnel reverse-forwards
  `$D/cold<i>.sock` to each GPU side's port. Any failure kills what was
  started and logs `no forwarded GPU this session, the host renders in
  software`. `supervise` kills them with the session.
* **Host, root.** `sv-hostd broker --listen /run/sv-hostd/broker.sock
  --socket-gid <gid>`: a root daemon on a group-only socket. A request names a
  directory exactly `/tmp/wc-launch/<id>` and a count; the directory and every
  `cold<i>.sock` must be the **peer's** by `SO_PEERCRED`, the directory not
  writable by others; then the broker runs `qemu-serve … --drop-to <peer
  uid>:<peer gid>`, relays its lines until it listens, and takes the next
  request — QMP serves one client. A child that does not listen in 180 s is
  killed. Unprivileged here, it refused a missing cold socket, `..`, a count of
  9 and a mode-777 directory, and ran `qemu-serve` against the peer's directory
  otherwise. It has not run as root. The operator starts it; one way, until
  nix-config has a unit for it:
  ```
  sudokey run -- systemd-run --unit=sv-hostd-broker -p RuntimeDirectory=sv-hostd \
    -p RuntimeDirectoryMode=0750 -p Group=wc-arena \
    ~/wc-launch-ivs/bin/sv-hostd broker --listen /run/sv-hostd/broker.sock \
    --socket-gid $(getent group wc-arena | cut -d: -f3)
  ```
* **Host, user.** `wc-session gpu ID N` checks the cold sockets and runs
  `sv-hostd broker-request`; `run` applies `gpu.env` **only** when this session
  has `$D/icd.sock`, adds `SV_SOCKET=$D/icd.sock`, and otherwise prints `NO GPU
  … Firefox renders in software` and applies nothing — a forced Zink with nothing
  behind it is a Firefox that cannot start its renderer. Tested by hand on the
  workstation both ways.
* **Decode.** `scripts/sv-firefox-readback-pkg.sh OBJDIR` turns the
  readback-patched `./mach` tree into a store path with a real closure (the
  stock wrapper retargeted, so the patched browser gets ffmpeg 9 and
  libpulseaudio exactly as stock does) and a marker,
  `lib/firefox/.wc-vulkan-readback`. When the session has a GPU and the
  resolved Firefox carries the marker, `run` adds the three
  `media.hardware-video-decoding-vulkan.*` prefs and
  `MOZ_DISABLE_RDD_SANDBOX=1`. Name it with `WC_LAUNCH_FIREFOX=<store
  path>/bin/firefox`. Built: `/nix/store/rk9rz146p8a31ffrd76pxbck4dn4pxjk-firefox-readback-157.0.1`
  (2.7 GiB closure, `--version` says 157.0.1).
* **Deploy.** `WC_LAUNCH_GPU_SESSIONS=N` builds `sv-guest.exe` with its GPU
  half (release), copies release `sv-hostd` and `libsv_icd.so` and writes
  `bin/sv_icd.json`; `gpu.env` is written only with `WC_LAUNCH_GPU_ENV=write`
  and `WC_LAUNCH_KOPPER_MESA`, and otherwise printed.

**The cost the broker carries, in security-model.md R30:** the dropped
`qemu-serve` holds QEMU's memory backend, so the peer can open all of guest RAM
through `/proc/<pid>/fd/<n>`. Membership of the broker's group is access to the
VM's memory.

On the merged tree (master d9b3a27 in), at the commit that adds this section:

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` (`CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4`, a copied Wine prefix) | **99 binaries, 2781 passed, 0 failed**, 8 ignored (master: 2770 at 98 binaries; the 11 new are `fault`'s 1, the broker's 3, `wc-launch`'s 7 across audio, config and plan) |

| `bash -n` on `wc-session`, `wc-launch.sh`, `sv-firefox-guest.sh`, `sv-firefox-readback-pkg.sh` | clean |
| Miri | not run: the new `unsafe` is FFI (waveOut, `SetUnhandledExceptionFilter`, `setresuid`, `SO_PEERCRED`), which Miri does not model |

On the real machines, each once unless the table says otherwise:

| run | result |
|---|---|
| `sv-firefox-guest.sh 2 60 probe`, stock Mesa | Zink on Intel UHD, Wayland platform; sv-hostd dropped to uid 1000 |
| the same, `mesa-kopper-wayland` 26.2.4 | Zink on Intel UHD, Mesa 26.2.4 |
| `sv-firefox-guest.sh 4 120 zink`, Firefox 157 (×5) | GPU-side fault in `igvk64.dll` ×4 (86.4); software WebRender ×1 under `SV_TRACE=pre` |
| `layout-probe.exe` in the guest | 86.4's table; **followed by the VM stopping** (86.5) |
| `wc-launch.sh deploy` to `wcivs` (×4) | 11 passed, 0 failed each time |
| `wc-launch.exe firefox` in session 0, the tone page | 63.4 s played, all audible, 0 dropped, 2 underruns (86.6) |
| the first audio route, ssh.exe stdout into a pipe | nothing delivered (86.6) |

### 86.9 What remains for "Firefox fully works on Windows"

1. **The Intel driver fault** (86.4). Fixed on our side, proven on a local
   driver, then one guest run of the `zink` harness — not of `layout-probe`.
2. **A present across the VM**: the `fence … ms` of firefox-accel.md, never
   measured because no frame was presented on the GPU. The ring waits in 86.3
   say the doorbell (§36.16) will be needed for a usable frame rate; its port is
   a QMP hot-add, which was not done.
3. **Accelerated Firefox through the launcher**: the broker run as root on
   testhost (a unit in nix-config on top of 102f747, after a dry-activate),
   `gpu.env`, `gpu-sessions = 4`, and the session-1 run; and a decision on R30.
4. **Hardware decode on the guest** (video-decode.md §7.9): every step, starting
   with whether the Intel driver takes a bitstream buffer in host-pointer-
   imported guest RAM. Nothing ran (GPU work was suspended).
5. **The session-1 run**: deploy, install, cold, warm, verify and shot on the
   ivshmem path with tabs in the title bar, the photographs (window, taskbar
   icon, title, tabs in the caption, about:support's Graphics and Media, a
   scrolled page) each judged by a visual-check agent, §85.10's guest list, and
   sound heard by a person: the sound path in session 1, with the user's own
   device.
6. **Troubleshoot Mode after an ended session** (86.6): a launcher session that
   ends under Firefox counts as a startup crash; three in a row put a modal
   dialog in front of the next start. Either the session end stops Firefox
   cleanly, or the deployment sets `toolkit.startup.max_resumed_crashes`.
7. **Audio delay and drift** (86.6, not measured), and sound for a second
   application in the same session (one sink, mixed; untested).
8. **The persistent VM change** (§83.9 item 2) is still not booted.
9. **The guest's LAN.** At the end of this work the guest answered on the
   host-only link (<guest-nat-ip>) and not on <guest-ip>: its adapter
   "Ethernet 2" had fallen back to an APIPA address (169.254.171.236). Nothing
   here touched networking, and this section does not know when it happened
   or why; it is reported, not changed.

## 87. The GPU sessions' arena on a second ivshmem device: no root for the GPU, a doorbell that crosses, and two faults found on the guest

Written 2026-10-15, on branch `gpu-guest`, from master 0ffe238. The brief: hardware
acceleration on the real guest with no root anywhere in the launch path, the
doorbell §86 left out, accelerated Firefox, hardware decode, and the Troubleshoot
Mode prompt. In order: the decision (87.2), whether Intel's driver takes an
ivshmem BAR (87.3), the guest and host halves (87.4), the doorbell (87.5),
accelerated Firefox (87.6), decode and the two faults it found (87.7), the
Troubleshoot prompt (87.8), what was deployed (87.9), the gates (87.10) and what
remains (87.11). Nobody was logged in to the guest, so every guest run was in
session 0, over ssh; nothing here was photographed.

### 87.1 Status in one paragraph

**The GPU path needs no root and no broker.** The GPU sessions' arena is BAR2 of
a second ivshmem device (256 MiB, slot 0x1d, `/run/windows-vm/wc-arena/gpu`,
`0660 root:wc-arena`); one guest process maps it and serves each session in its
own 80 MiB slot; the host's `sv-hostd ivshmem-serve` runs in a user unit as
`sirati` and refuses to run as root. Intel's Windows driver **imports a pointer
into the BAR** with `VK_EXT_external_memory_host` and the GPU reads and writes it
exactly. The doorbell port is hot-added and works once its Windows handle is
opened overlapped: vulkaninfo's mean ring wait fell from **10.18 ms to 0.017
ms**. Firefox 157 on Zink on the guest's Intel UHD ran a **340 s** tour with
`Compositing WebRender`, the present's fence at **2.09 ms** and **40.4 fps**
while scrolling. `video-probe` decoded H.264 through the forwarder
byte-identically to libavcodec (`b3a1374e…`). That run then ended with **a fault
in `igvk64.dll`** — caused by this branch's own slot cleanup destroying a command
pool a second time — and by the rule of §86.5 GPU work on the guest stopped
there. The cause is fixed and proven on RADV and NVIDIA (87.7); the fixed build
has not run on the guest, so the launcher's GPU is **not** switched on (87.9).

### 87.2 The decision: a second device, one process, slots

§86 measured each GPU session at 80 MiB (16 MiB control region + a 64 MiB arena)
and Firefox wanting several. Two facts about an ivshmem device settle the shape.
**Its driver gives the BAR to one handle** (§83.5), so one guest process maps it
and every session is a slice. **The doorbell's port takes one opener** (§36's
`vdoorbell` header), the same answer from the other side. And a session that
ends must give its slot back, because Firefox's `glxtest` takes one and exits
before the browser asks for its own.

So: a second device rather than carving the compositor's 128 MiB, which is twice
§28.12's peak and has no room; 256 MiB rather than 512, because testhost had
1363 MiB available before the hot-plug and 1090 after it (`free -m`), and three
concurrent sessions cover `glxtest`, the GPU process and an RDD or a restart.
`sv-gpu-server guest --ivshmem-slot 0x1d` (`crates/sv-gpu-server/src/ivshmem.rs`,
`entry.rs::win_guest_ivshmem`) maps the device **by slot** — the instance path's
last component is the devfn, `&E8` for 0x1d — accepts one TCP connection per
session on one port, and gives each the lowest free slot: stamped as the
guest-RAM path stamped it, offered with `Locator::Ivshmem { region_offset }`, its
own `VkDevice`, its own import of its slot's arena. `wc_handle::map_ivshmem`
sorts the interfaces now, so the compositor's `--arena-ivshmem 0` is still the
device at 0x1c with two present.

### 87.3 Does Intel's driver take a BAR mapping as a host pointer? Yes

§83.2 kept guest-RAM arenas for shared_vulkan because a BAR is `VM_IO|VM_PFNMAP`
to Linux's pinning path. Whether the *Windows* driver pins a user mapping of an
I/O-space MDL was the open question. `sv-ivshmem-probe` (in
`crates/sv-gpu-server/src/bin/`) asked it in three steps, each opt-in past the
first, on the hot-plugged device, nothing else running:

| step | result |
|---|---|
| `vkGetMemoryHostPointerPropertiesEXT`, heap pointer (control) | `SUCCESS`, `memoryTypeBits 0x6` |
| the same, BAR pointer (+1 MiB) | `SUCCESS`, `0x6`; `minImportedHostPointerAlignment 4096` |
| `--import`: `vkAllocateMemory` of 4 MiB of the BAR | **ok**, memory type 1 (`DEVICE_LOCAL\|HOST_VISIBLE\|HOST_COHERENT`), 104 µs |
| GPU copy BAR → device-local → BAR (2 × 2 MiB) + `vkCmdFillBuffer` | **0 of 524288 words wrong**, 1.18 ms; best of 5, 0.72 ms (5.8 GB/s) |
| the filled page in `/run/windows-vm/wc-arena/gpu`, read by `sirati` on the host | all 1024 words `PGVS`; the copied words at their offsets (`53564750 cd613ee1 …`) |

So no staging copy is needed. Its price was measured anyway (`--staging`, 4 MiB,
best of 5): BAR → driver-allocated cached memory 0.27 ms and back 0.26 ms
(15.7 GB/s); to write-combined memory 0.28 ms, and **29.2 ms** back out of it,
which is what reading WC costs. A session's device, its 64 MiB import and its
control region took 93–224 ms on the guest; the host's check of a slot's 20480
stamped pages, 116–343 ms.

**Not measured:** whether the import keeps working across a guest driver reset,
and whether a BAR import costs the GPU anything per access that guest RAM does
not (Firefox's numbers in 87.6 are the only comparison, and §86 never had one).

### 87.4 The two halves, and the run that found the ordering

**Guest.** One process, `sv-guest.exe gpu guest --port P --ivshmem-slot 0x1d
--sessions N --bell org.sirati.svbell.0`. A session ends 5 s after its
application's heartbeat stops (`session::APP_GONE_AFTER`): `wait_until`'s own
liveness check started a fresh 600 ms window on each 50 ms call and never fired,
so an exited application had only been noticed by the 120 s idle limit, which
with slots is a slot `glxtest` keeps from the browser. A slot whose application
destroyed everything is released; one with leftovers has them destroyed first
(`Objects::destroy_leftovers`, children before parents, never the arena's own
memory, nothing at all if an unhandled type such as a video session is left, in
which case the slot is quarantined). Measured on vulkaninfo ×4 in one process:
slots 0, 1, 0, 1, each `released`.

**Host.** `sv-hostd ivshmem-serve --region … --cold $D/cold.sock --socket
$D/icd.sock [--bell … --bell-hub $D/bell.sock]`, started by `wc-session gpu ID N`
in the user unit `wc-launch-gpu-ID`. Per ICD: connect to the guest through the
tunnel's one forward, take the `Hello`, read every stamped page of the slot,
`Accept`, **wait for the guest's `Ping`**, and hand the ICD the file's path and
the slot's offsets. The ICD opens the file itself, by name (docs/design.md §1a).

**The `Ping` is the run that found the ordering.** The first vulkaninfo was
refused by the ICD with `magic is 0x31414e4552415653` — `SVARENA1`, the stamp.
On guest RAM every session was located before any ICD existed, so its control
region was always published by the time one attached; here the ICD is what asks
for the session, and it read the control header while the guest was still
opening its device. The guest now says `Ping` after `Control::create`, or
`Refuse` with the reason.

**One deployment fact, not a code one.** The first launcher run's proxy got
`Permission denied` on `/run/windows-vm/wc-arena/arena`: `sirati`'s systemd user
manager predates generation 51, which added the user to `wc-arena`, so user units
run without the group (`/proc/<pid>/status`: `Groups: 1 57 100 302`). The VM's
17:44 start recreated the file without §83's ACL. The files and the bell socket
were given `u:sirati:rw` by ACL, as §83 did; the next login or reboot makes that
unnecessary.

### 87.5 The doorbell: hot-added, and a Windows handle that serialised it

`chardev-add` of a server socket `/run/windows-vm/wc-arena/svbell.sock` and
`device_add virtserialport,bus=vioserial.0,chardev=svbell,name=org.sirati.svbell.0`
on the running VM, then `chgrp wc-arena` and `chmod 0660` on the socket, which
QEMU had made `root 0755`. The guest opened the port by name at once, as §36.16
found for a fresh port.

**The first run with it hung, and the cause was ours.** vulkaninfo's first
`vkCreateInstance` waited 3 × 10 s and died `DEVICE_LOST`; without the bell it
ran. `winpipe::open_virtio_port` opened the port synchronously, and **the I/O
manager serialises every call on a synchronous handle**: the doorman sat in
`ReadFile`, so the first reply's `WriteFile` — the bell — waited behind it, and
the ring thread that rang it served nothing more. `sv-bell-probe` never met this
because it reads and writes from one thread in turn. Ports are now opened
`FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`, each call with its own `OVERLAPPED`.

**One port, every session.** A byte carries a ring slot and a lane but not a
session, so the guest rings it in every live session (`vdoorbell::ControlSet`)
and the host's hub (`sv_hostd::ivshmem::bell_hub`) holds QEMU's one chardev
connection and passes bytes to and from every ICD. The session it was for wakes;
the rest see a spurious wake, which §36.6.4 already prices at a syscall.

| | ring waits | parked | mean | histogram |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| vulkaninfo, no doorbell | 2357 | 23,994 ms | **10.18 ms** | `<100us=666 <1ms=160 <10ms=598 <100ms=932` |
| vulkaninfo, doorbell (×5) | 2356–2357 | 33–42 ms | **0.014–0.018 ms** | `<10us=2257…2288 <100us≈30 <1ms≈50` |
| Firefox, guest without its port (control) | — | — | — | Marionette's `NewSession` had not returned at 120 s |

PUSH_DESCRIPTOR set layout with non-zero binding flags will be refused`). A

So the cross-VM present costs about 2 ms of a frame at 1228×848, against
§0.28.8's 0.7 ms on one machine; the frame rate while scrolling is 40 fps, not

present, not where a frame's time goes. **Not measured:** the interactive

### 87.7 Decode, and the two faults it found

**Capabilities through the forwarder**, three runs: the GPU process died each
time partway through `video-probe caps`, inside a different
`vkGetPhysicalDeviceVideoFormatPropertiesKHR` each run (`SV_TRACE=pre`),
printing nothing — the fault handler never ran. A wrapper that waits for the
process gave the reason: **exit code `0xC0000374`, `STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION`**.
The API dump of the same forwarded calls on RADV and NVIDIA is well formed. So
every allocation the forwarder hands a driver now carries 256 bytes of canary
(`sv_gpu_entry::Raise`, `guard_spare` / `check_spare` for output arrays, emitted
by the generator), and the next run said, once:

```
[gpu] GUARD: the driver wrote past a sv_icd_entry::VkVideoDecodeCapabilitiesKHR:
      4 of the 256 guard bytes after it changed
```

Intel's `vkGetPhysicalDeviceVideoCapabilitiesKHR` writes four bytes past
`VkVideoDecodeCapabilitiesKHR`. The in-guest `video-probe.exe` of video-decode.md
§1 has the struct on its stack, where four bytes go unnoticed. With the guard
every profile answered as that survey did — H.264 baseline to high interlaced,
H.265 main and main10, AV1 8- and 10-bit supported, AV1 with film grain
`ERROR_VIDEO_PROFILE_CODEC_NOT_SUPPORTED_KHR` — except that the decode family has
one queue through the forwarder and two on the driver, because the GPU side
opens one.

**The decode**, video-decode.md §7.9's step 3:

```
memory: bitstream buffer 8192 B, bits 0xe -> type 1 HOST_VISIBLE | HOST_COHERENT
decoded 24 frames of 320x180 (coded 320x192) as G8_B8R8_2PLANE_420_UNORM on Intel(R) UHD Graphics
decode submit->fence: median 1.027 ms over 24 frames
b3a1374ee5f09350b022a225b35528b6549af33fc025db08fd224b232e9a187a  out.nv12
```

**Byte-identical to libavcodec**, and §7.9's first question is answered: Intel
takes a bitstream buffer with `VIDEO_DECODE_SRC` bound into host-pointer-imported
memory, here a BAR.

**Then `igvk64.dll` faulted**, after `video-probe` had exited, in the slot
cleanup:

```
[gpu] FAULT: exception 0xc0000005 at 0x7ff92d1003e8 in …\iigd_dch.inf_amd64_a8d32ac2abbe057a\igvk64.dll+0xf03e8
[gpu] FAULT: read of 0x1345712e1a8
  ring 1: seqno 21 vkDestroyInstance (returned)   ring 2: seqno 191 vkDestroyDevice (returned)
  12: <sv_gpu_server::table::Objects>::destroy_leftovers
```

The guest stayed up (ssh and ping before and after); QEMU logged the iGPU going
D0→D3 and `guest disables memory decode … unmapping the BARs before the host
does`, which is generation 51's patch doing its job. **By §86.5's rule GPU work
on the guest stopped here**, and the cause was found and fixed locally:

- The generator's parent list — `VkCommandPool` and `VkDescriptorPool`, so that
  `vkFreeCommandBuffers` does not unbind the pool its buffers came from — also
  kept **`vkDestroyCommandPool` and `vkDestroyDescriptorPool` from unbinding the
  pool they destroy**. Every destroyed pool stayed in the table. The API dump
  showed `video-probe` destroying both of its command pools; the table still
  held them; `destroy_leftovers` destroyed them again. A `vkDestroyX` now
  unbinds its `X` (`sv-codegen`, `emit/gpu_entry.rs`). `glxtest`'s "8 command
  pools" in 87.6 were, by the same reading, destroyed twice on Intel three times
  without a fault.
- Proven without the guest: the local serve path prints each session's
  leftovers and, with `SV_DESTROY_LEFTOVERS=1`, destroys them. A Zink `gl-probe`
  session on RADV left 49 objects; every one was checked against the API dump as
  created after its handle's last destroy (handle reuse is real: one buffer
  address was destroyed and created again); all 49 were destroyed with the
  Khronos validation layer loaded and no message from the destruction.
  `video-probe` through the fixed forwarder leaves nothing. A unit test makes
  one object of every handled type on the local driver and destroys it.

**Not run, because GPU work on the guest stopped:** the fixed build on the
guest; ffmpeg through the forwarder (§7.9 step 4); the validation layer on the
guest (step 5); the readback Firefox with H.264 (step 6).

### 87.8 "Open Firefox in Troubleshoot Mode?"

`wc-session run` now writes `toolkit.startup.max_resumed_crashes = -1` into every
launcher profile's `user.js`. Measured in session 0 with the deployed `wcivs`
installation (software rendering, so not GPU work): five sessions each ended
with `wc-launch.exe --stop` under a running Firefox. Firefox still counts them —
`toolkit.startup.recent_crashes` went 1, 2, 3, 4 — but the fifth start, at 4,
past the default limit of 3, opened the browser: the compositor logged `title
-> "Restore Session — Mozilla Firefox"`, not the dialog. Cleaned on testhost:
the counter removed from all five launcher profiles' `prefs.js`, the pref added
to the three `user.js` files that lacked it, and a stale `lock` in
`ff-h264exp` (pid 1580081, not running) removed. **Not changed:** the "Restore
Session" page each such start shows; `browser.sessionstore.resume_from_crash`
would hide it and would also throw away the tabs of a real crash.

3e4f6ad): the prepare step gives every `waycomposeArena.members` entry

start. `dry-activate`: only `windows-vm.service`, "would NOT stop"; `switch`:

carries `lib/firefox/.wc-vulkan-readback`. The deployed launcher does not use it
(it runs `firefox`, which resolves to the stock 157), so decode stays off there.

**H.264 in Firefox on the guest, once** (the test installation, the readback
Firefox, a 1280×720 H.264 High clip looped every 10 s): Firefox chose the
Vulkan decoder on the guest's GPU (`Selected Vulkan device for video decoding:
Intel(R) UHD Graphics (vendorID=0x8086, deviceID=0xa7a8)`, `[VULKAN] readback:
decoded frames are copied to host memory`) and the RDD log has **1145**
`[VULKAN] readback: 1280x720 frame copied to host memory` lines; the page counted
1147 frames, 40 dropped, `err=none`, for 38 s. Then the GPU side faulted:

```
[gpu] FAULT: exception 0xc0000005 at 0x7ff92d30185b in …\igvk64.dll+0x2f185b
[gpu] FAULT: read of 0x7c
  ring 1: seqno 368 vkGetPhysicalDeviceImageFormatProperties2 (returned)
  ring 2: seqno 48482 vkWaitForFences (returned)   ring 3: seqno 4654 vkQueueSubmit (returned)
  20: <sv_gpu_entry::Forward<…GpuServer> as sv_proto::Server>::cmd_decode_video_khr
  22: sv_proto::subdecode   23: sv_gpu_server::session::drain
```

— inside Intel's `vkCmdDecodeVideoKHR`, replayed from a command blob, with the
page then at `err=3` (decode). The last readback lines come from a second
decoder instance (`MediaPDecoder #2`), so the fault came around the clip's fourth
loop. The VM stayed up; QEMU logged the iGPU going D0→D3 with the BARs unmapped
first. **By §86.5's rule GPU work on the guest stopped**, and so did this
section's guest steps: no about:support Media evidence was captured (the
driver's snapshot would have come after the clip), and decode is **not** enabled

frames on RADV with the usual 96 MiB arena and 2155 with the guest's 64 MiB, no
error; the dumped `vkCmdDecodeVideoKHR`s are well formed (bitstream buffer and
range, a setup slot, three reference slots, each with an image view). A read of
`0x7c` is a null structure's field, so the first suspect is an argument the
forwarder hands Intel as null only when ffmpeg re-initialises a decoder; that is
an inference from the address, not a finding.

**Not run, by the same rule**: ffmpeg through the forwarder and the validation
layer on the guest (video-decode.md §7.9 steps 4–5).

### 87.13 Follow-up: the decode fault, found and fixed; decode on in the launcher

Branch `decode-capture`, 2026-10-15. The detail is video-decode.md §7.11.
Six guest runs, each authorised, all in session 0, with health checks every
15 s. The VM never stopped: QEMU was pid 230263 from 17:44 to the end.

- **Feature chain (fixed).** The GPU side's device now enables every feature
  struct of every enabled extension, from the registry, and answers
  `vkGetPhysicalDeviceFeatures2` with what it enabled. Zink had been using
  `VK_EXT_extended_dynamic_state3` and six other feature sets that were never
  enabled: a 120 s Firefox soak under GPU-side validation went from 395
  errors to 0. Drivers are opened and closed under one process-wide lock
  (two concurrent opens crashed the Vulkan loader).
- **The decode fault (fixed).** Intel's `igvk64.dll` 101.7076 follows
  pointers into structures it was handed by *earlier*
  `vkCmdBeginVideoCodingKHR`/`vkCmdDecodeVideoKHR` calls, at a mid-stream IDR.
  Native ffmpeg keeps those structures in recycled per-picture memory, which
  hides this; the forwarder freed its copies after each call. The evidence:
  - the capture run and the view-cache run faulted at the packet-250 IDR;
  - the second minidump shows our own guard bytes behind the stale pointer;
  - a run keeping every call's structures alive did not fault.

  The fix keeps the decode structures in per-slot stores that live as long as
  the session. The confirmation run: 3029 decodes, ten of the formerly fatal
  IDRs, no fault.
- **Decode on in `wcivs`.** The deployed launcher runs the readback Firefox
  with the decode prefs. On this driver the GPU side serves H.264 decode
  only, and H.265, AV1 and VP9 fall back to software, cleanly. One playback
  through it: about:support Media `H264 … Hardware Decoding Supported`.

### 87.14 Follow-up: H.265 decode on in the launcher; AV1 and VP9 stay in software

Branch `decode-codecs`, 2026-10-15 and 16. The detail is video-decode.md
§7.12. Two guest runs, both authorised, both in session 0, with health checks
every 15 s (41 samples, all good). QEMU never stopped, and nothing faulted.

- **What the driver offers.** Intel 101.7076 answers H.264 and H.265 with
  COINCIDE output and 16 and 15 DPB slots. It answers AV1 with **8 slots**,
  refuses AV1 film grain, and has no VP9 extension. The GPU side now asks
  each codec's basic profile itself and prints what it serves.
- **H.265 (on).** The per-slot, session-lifetime stores of §87.13 now cover
  H.265 and AV1 as well as H.264, as ffmpeg's per-picture memory does. The
  SPS, PPS and VPS arrays are kept for the session's life. On the test
  installation, 3029 H.265 decodes over 12 IDRs, 1214 H.264 decodes, 0
  findings, no fault.
- **AV1 (withheld).** A real AV1 stream needs 9 slots: 8 references and the
  picture being decoded. With 8, ffmpeg uses slot index 8 anyway, and RADV
  shaped to 8 slots gave wrong frames with no error. No remapping on our side
  can fit those streams into 8. So AV1 is withheld on any driver with fewer
  than 9 slots, and on the guest it plays in software: the YouTube 720p60
  clip played with `err=none` and lost 41% of its frames on testhost's CPU.
  Through the stores, at 9 slots, AV1 is byte-identical to libavcodec (RADV).
- **A slot guard.** A decode naming a slot beyond its session is never
  handed to the driver. Its command buffer fails to submit and Firefox falls
  back to software. That fixed three faults in poisoning: the marks were per
  ring, a refused end left the driver's buffer recording, and a refused
  submit left ffmpeg waiting for a fence forever.
- **Deployed.** `wcivs` was backed up (`C:\Users\<guest-user>\wcivs-backup-712`,
  `~/wc-launch-ivs-backup-712`), then redeployed from d113d80: 12 passed, 0
  failed. One playback through it: HEVC, 1200 frames, `err=none`, 1209
  frames decoded on the GPU. about:support Media: `H264` and `HEVC` with
  hardware decoding Supported; `AV1`, `VP9` and `VP8` without. The
  temporary Marionette and log settings were removed; the ini and `gpu.env`
  are byte-identical to the deployed ones.
