### 103.13 One main process and a face per application (supersedes 103.8's "one compositor per application")

The user replaced 103.8's per-application compositors. Now **one main
process per user** holds everything there is one of: the smithay/Wayland
state, the arena, the session with the host, the clipboard, the keyboard
layout, idle inhibition and the policy. **One small face process per Linux
application** exists only because a Dock tile is a process. It owns that
application's `NSApplication` (the tile, the Dock menu, the menu bar,
activation) and its `NSWindow`s, and it forwards input and window events.
The faces have no arena, no proxy and no session of their own.

**Pixels: IOSurfaces sent by mach port.** Measured first, on the Sonoma VM,
between two processes of the user's GUI session:

| way to share an IOSurface | result |
|---|---|
| `kIOSurfaceIsGlobal` + `IOSurfaceLookup(id)` | works; rejected, because any process that guesses a 32-bit id maps the pixels, and Apple deprecated it |
| `IOSurfaceCreateMachPort` sent through `bootstrap_check_in` of an undeclared name, `IOSurfaceLookupFromMachPort` | works (`check_in ok`, same bytes on both sides); **chosen**. The name exists only in this user's GUI bootstrap namespace, and the port is a capability only the receiving face holds |
| a full 1280x720 copy into an IOSurface | 0.054 ms |

The main process keeps a **ping-pong pair** of IOSurfaces per window. On each
present it copies the compositor's shadow into the back surface (one CPU copy,
the 0.054 ms above for a full frame) and tells the face which surface to show.
The face sets that IOSurface as its layer's `contents`, and Core Animation and
WindowServer read it directly: **no copy in the face, none in Core
Animation**. The pair means the main process never writes the surface on
screen. Composing straight into the IOSurface, rather than into the shadow,
would remove the last copy; that is not built. A face mapping the arena itself
was rejected: a `CALayer` cannot show raw memory without a `CGImage`, and
that is a copy per frame in Core Animation.

**IPC.** A Unix socket at `$TMPDIR/waycompose/main.sock`: `$TMPDIR` is per
user, the directory is 0700, the socket 0600, and every connection's peer uid
is checked with `getpeereid`. The messages are `faceproto.rs` (window commands
one way, input, window events, popup bounds, Dock-menu requests and a goodbye
the other), length-prefixed, with one writer thread per side, so input stays in
order. A surface pair's mach message is sent **before** the socket message that
names it, so the face finds the ports already queued and ordering needs no
second protocol. Measured from AppKit's event timestamp in the face to arrival
in the main process: 100 events, **p50 1.7 ms, p90 7.2 ms, max 33 ms** (the
timestamp has 1 ms resolution, and the VM is running Firefox in software
alongside).

**Routing.** A window goes to a face when it maps: the face whose ids
(`faceproto::face_ids`: the section, the host's id, the desktop entry's name,
its `StartupWMClass`) match its `app_id`. Failing that, the face that most
recently asked to run something, then the focused face. Popups go to their
parent's face. The main process keeps every window's state (title, icons, size
hints, map, maximise, fullscreen), so a face can be given its windows again.

**Lifecycle.**
* A bundle launch starts a face. The face connects to the socket, and if
  nothing listens it starts the main process (`wc-launch --main`, from the
  installed binary, in its own process group). It then says hello with its
  ids and a token, sends its own mach port to the main process's service with
  the same token, and asks to run its application. The main process brings the
  session up once and queues requests until it is up.
* **A face that crashes** (no goodbye) has its windows kept. The main process
  starts it again (`open -g -b`, with retries) and replays its windows when it
  says hello. Measured: `kill -9` of Firefox's face, face 3 came back, window 1
  was routed to it, and Firefox showed its window again fully drawn, while
  Console was untouched. If the face does not come back within 15 s, the
  windows' clients are asked to close.
* **A main process that crashes** takes the faces down: their sockets end and
  they quit (measured: both faces gone within 1 s of `kill -9`). Its ssh
  tunnel and the host's proxy outlive it, so the next main process kills the
  recorded tunnel pid (only if it is still an `ssh`) and sends `down` for the
  recorded session. Measured: the stale session disappeared from the host.
* **Quit** (Cmd+Q, AppleScript, the Dock) closes the face's windows, and the
  face leaves as soon as they are gone (measured: 1 s). The main process ends
  when its last client has gone, or after 60 s with no face.
* The main process uses `NSApplicationActivationPolicyProhibited`: no tile
  and no menu bar of its own. A face registers as a regular application before
  it does anything else. A face that waited for the main process first was
  left behind Finder: the activation that LaunchServices sends with the launch
  found no application yet, and macOS 14's cooperative activation refused the
  later request. The face's first window also calls
  `activateIgnoringOtherApps`.

**Each bundle has its own copy of the launcher, not a hard link.** Measured:
with every bundle's executable the same inode, LaunchServices took a second
application for the first one already running. Console did not start while
Firefox ran. A relaunch of Firefox's face failed with `procNotFound`, because
the main process, running from the same inode, was taken for Firefox. 103.8's
earlier "two applications at once" row was therefore wrong, as written: Console
had started only after Firefox had quit. With copies, Firefox and Console run
side by side (two faces, two tiles, one session).

**Arena per session, pluggable.** There is one arena per main process,
shared by every application. Guest RAM by default (role (a)); with
`WC_MAC_ARENA_STANDIN=<file>`, a shared file that the compositor maps as its
"ivshmem" device, with `up ID RUNID ivshmem` on the host. That is role (b)'s
hook: on the real Mac, the RAM-disk file shared with the Linux guest through
virtio-fs DAX. The role (b) path was not run here.

Re-tested under the split, in the 4 GiB VM, each image judged by a fresh Sonnet
agent:
* Firefox from its tile, maximised, fully drawn from the IOSurfaces, with the
  traffic lights beside the tabs.
* Console as a second application alongside it.
* The Dock menu's New Window routed back to Firefox's face.
* The clipboard both ways: 24 bytes exact to Linux, and the string back
  through `pbpaste`.
* A context menu routed to the parent's face, fully drawn.
* Sound played by the main process: 4.7 s of 438 Hz tone with one 10 ms gap.
* The crash cases above.

Known: GNOME Console shows a native title bar *and* GTK 4's header bar, which
is GTK 4 negotiating server-side decorations under the compositor's `Auto`.

**Still on ssh at this commit, and therefore open (103.14 then replaced it):**
the Wayland bytes (an ssh Unix-socket forward), the session control (`up`,
`proxy`, `run`, `down` as ssh exec), the sound (an ssh `-L` forward of the
PulseAudio monitor), and the icon and clipboard feeds, which ride the Wayland
upstream.

### 103.14 Nothing on ssh: the session's channels on rings in guest RAM

The user's rule: on macOS nothing travels over ssh, TCP or a socket forward.
The premise is shared memory, and an ssh path is a defect, not a milestone.
103.4's Unix-socket forward, the sound's `-L` forward and the session control
by ssh exec are gone from the steady state.

**The ring region.** With `--wayland-rings-guest-ram`, the main process's
compositor keeps a second window of its own RAM, `Geometry::for_wayland()`
(6 MiB, 32 slots). It is stamped like the arena (`stamped_guest_ram_window`)
and located once by the host (`wc-session rings`, which runs `wc-arena-host`).
After the locate, the launcher signals `guest_ram_rings_located`, and the
compositor makes the shared_vulkan control region in it. The proxy attaches it
from the plan (`--wayland-rings-plan`, retrying until the region is made).
Separate from the arena, so the arena's allocator is untouched. The same
`Control`/`ByteChannel` code runs over any region, which is what keeps the
transport independent of the backend: role (b) attaches the same control region
in its shared DAX file, by name.

**Its slots.**
* Every Wayland connection is a slot.
* The **icon and clipboard feeds**, which until now always used the upstream
  socket (§36.8: "a second ring claim, not built"), now claim slots of their
  own. A local socket pair is bridged to each slot (`rings::bridge`), so the
  feed code is unchanged.
* The **control** channel (`OWNER_CONTROL`) carries `run`/`action`/`open`/`down`
  as the words `wc-session` takes. The proxy runs `wc-session` itself on them
  (`macsvc.rs`), with the session id put first by the host, so §94's
  validation is the same code as on the ssh path.
* The **sound** channel (`OWNER_AUDIO`) carries the session's PulseAudio
  monitor.
* Service slots carry an owner-id tag (`wlbytes::SERVICE_TAG`) that the
  compositor's accept skips. These additions to sv-transport (`ring_owner`, the
  tags) are additive.

**Liveness.** The guest's RAM is the guest's. When the main process dies, macOS
frees those pages and reuses them, so a proxy still writing pixels or ring bytes
would corrupt them. The main process sends `ping` on the control channel every
500 ms. After the first ping, 5 s without one ends the proxy before it touches
the region again. Measured: `kill -9` of the main process; the proxy logged
`LEASE LOST` and was gone about 4 s later. **The lease was not enough**: in
those seconds the proxy wrote into pages macOS had already reused, and the
guest kernel panicked (103.15, which adds the keeper).

**Doorbells** (attached since 103.15). This VM had no doorbell port yet, so both sides polled the rings
every millisecond: the compositor's wait is capped at 1 ms, and the proxy's
`Doorbell::polling` wakes each waiting pump every millisecond. The endpoint stays
pluggable for the real doorbell: `--wayland-bell` takes a QEMU chardev socket
(the §99 hub, Linux/Windows hosts), the macOS guest opens a `/dev/cu.*` node
(`PortHandle::guest_port`), and a fd pair (role (b), libkrun's virtio-console
ports) is the third. The fd pair is not built. Measured cost of polling with
Firefox idle: the main process 11% of one vCPU, the proxy 2.8%.

**What ssh still did, once per main process: the bootstrap (gone since 103.15).** Three ssh execs
under the forced command: `up` (locate the arena), `rings` (locate the ring
region), `proxy` (start the proxy on them). After a main process that crashed,
the next one also sends `down` for the stale session. Nothing is forwarded, and
nothing goes over ssh afterwards. A bootstrap with no ssh at all would need the
host to find a new session's stamps by itself (a rendezvous magic in the sweep),
or a doorbell port to carry the hello as the Linux guest's cold path does. That
is open (103.12).

**Measured: rings against the old ssh path.** The same proxy and a C client
(`wl_display_roundtrip` 500 times, client to proxy to compositor and back).
The ssh leg is `scripts/mac-window.sh`, whose upstream is the ssh Unix-socket
forward and which is kept as the comparison leg:

| path | p50 | p90 | p99 | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ssh Unix-socket forward | 5.72 ms | 6.44 ms | 6.81 ms | 10.1 ms |
| rings in guest RAM, polled every 1 ms | **1.06 ms** | 2.12 ms | 2.14 ms | 2.15 ms |

The control channel's round trip for `run firefox` is 106 ms, of which 104 ms is
`wc-session` itself.

**Every channel, how it crosses, and its copies** (role (a), this VM):

| channel | crosses as | copies per transfer |
|---|---|---|
| Wayland bytes | ring slots in the guest-RAM ring region; no fds cross (in-band names, §79) | client socket to proxy (kernel); proxy into the ring (1); the compositor out of the ring into its local socket pair (1); smithay reads it (kernel) |
| `wl_shm` buffers, frames | the arena (guest RAM, located once) | proxy copies the client's damage into an arena slice (1, the only write across the boundary); compositor composes the slice into the window's shadow (1); main process copies the shadow into the back IOSurface (1, full frame); face and Core Animation show the IOSurface (0) |
| Vulkan | the GPU extent, wired guest RAM located once; the cold path (`Hello`, `Accept`) in the extent's first page (103.6.1), its rings in the same extent; no socket, forward or TCP (`lsof` on the server: 0 network and 0 Unix sockets) | frames: lavapipe renders into the imported extent, and the ICD reads them out of the same mapping (103.6) |
| control (`run`, `action`, `open`, `down`, lease) | the control ring slot | a line into the ring and back |
| sound | the sound ring slot | the monitor socket to proxy (kernel); proxy into the ring (1); main process out of the ring into its play queue (1); into an AudioQueue buffer (1) |
| clipboard | the clipboard feed's ring slot; NSPasteboard in the main process | bytes through the feed's socket pair and ring (2) |
| icons | the icon feed's ring slot | as the clipboard |
| face to main IPC | inside macOS: a 0600 Unix socket for messages; IOSurfaces by mach port for pixels | message bytes (kernel); pixels 0 |
| bootstrap | three ssh execs per main process (above) | not a data path |

Re-tested on rings, each image judged by a fresh Sonnet agent:
* Firefox from its tile, fully drawn.
* Clipboard both ways: `mac-to-linux-on-rings-55` pasted exactly into
  Firefox, and `linux-to-mac-on-rings-66` read back with `pbpaste`.
* The Dock menu's New Window routed back to Firefox's face (227 ms control
  round trip).
* The context menu, a separate child window, fully drawn.
* Console as a second application on the same rings.
* Sound: 6 s of ~431 Hz tone with 90 ms of gaps. The proxy dropped a few
  chunks on a full ring, most likely before the guest's player started.
* The lease.

**Still not on shared memory when 103.14 was written (all closed in 103.15):** the bootstrap's three ssh execs (and
the stale-session `down`), the GPU server's launch (`mac-gpu.sh` starts it over
ssh; a deployment would start it from `wc-launch` with a fixed label, 103.6.1),
and the doorbell (polled). The fd-pair doorbell exists in sv-transport
(`PortHandle` `fd:R,W`, 103.6.1) and the Wayland side does not use it yet.

**Evidence stays out of git.** No screenshot, image or log of this work is
committed. Screenshots, run logs and captures are under
`/mnt/datasets/builds/evidence/macos-host/` (`mac-last/`, `macgpu-last/`,
`mac-pin-*/`, `rtt/`), outside the repository, and this section states their
results in text. The harnesses write there (`WC_EVIDENCE` overrides it).

#### 103.14.1 The shared interfaces, for every platform

These are the pieces other platforms reuse (the Windows path without ssh,
host integration). None of them is macOS-specific code; the module names
`macsvc.rs`, `macboot.rs` and `mac-sessiond` are historical.

**Service slots** (`sv_transport::wlbytes`). A ring slot whose owner id has
`SERVICE_TAG` (`0x5C << 56`) in its top byte is a session service, not a
Wayland client, and the compositor's accept skips it (`is_service`). The host
claims each one; the guest opens it with `ByteChannel::open(.., Endpoint::Peer)`
once `ring_owner(slot)` names it. Allocated: `OWNER_CONTROL = SERVICE_TAG | 1`,
`OWNER_AUDIO = SERVICE_TAG | 2` (and the sound ring's further streams, if it
takes a slot per stream, as `SERVICE_TAG | 2 | n << 8`), `SERVICE_TAG | 3`
reserved for host integration (`OWNER_HOSTINT`).

**The control ring** (`OWNER_CONTROL`, host side `wc-proxy/src/macsvc.rs`).
Lines of UTF-8 ending in `\n`, one request and one reply each, in order:

| guest sends | host does | reply |
|---|---|---|
| `ping` | records the lease (no reply) | none |
| `run APP …`, `action APP KEY …`, `open APP URL …` | runs `wc-session` with the verb, then this session's id, then the guest's words, as `SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND`, so §94's validation is the forced command's | `ok <wc-session's stdout, newlines as "; "> (<n> ms)` or `err <stderr>` |
| `down` | replies, then the proxy exits; the session service runs `wc-session down` once the proxy's unit has ended (103.15) | `ok down` |

Requests are words of `[A-Za-z0-9 +/=._-]`, at most 16 KiB; anything else is
refused with `err refused: …`. The lease: after the first `ping`, 5 s without
one ends the proxy (exit 4). The guest pings every 500 ms.

**The boot record and the release word** (`wc_handle::macboot`, 103.15): page
0 of the guest's ring window, at offset 1024. The guest writes `WCMBOOT1`, the
version, a flags word (bit 0: the guest started a GPU server labelled with the
session id, cut to 16 bytes), the session id (64 bytes), the arena's run id,
page count and outbound bytes, and the ring window's run id and page count. The
host answers in the same page: a message (offset 1160, 512 bytes) and then the
state word (offset 1152: `Waiting`, `Located` or `Failed`), and at the end of
the session the release word (offset 1728). The control region starts at the
window's second page, so the boot page lives as long as the session.

**The session service** (`wc-arena-host mac-sessiond --qmp SOCK --vm HINT
--session WC-SESSION [--bell HUB-SOCKET] [--sweep-secs N]`, a user unit beside
the VM). It finds boot records, runs `up`, `rings`, `proxy` and (with the GPU
flag) `gpu` through `wc-session` with its unit's environment, answers in the
boot page, and when a session's proxy unit has ended runs `down` and writes the
release word. Its environment is what the forced command's `env` was
(`WC_LAUNCH_GUEST_RAM=1`, `WC_LAUNCH_QMP`, `WC_LAUNCH_VM`, `WC_LAUNCH_APPS`,
`WC_LAUNCH_MAC_BELL`, `WC_LAUNCH_MAC_GPU_BELL`, …). It remembers each live
session's boot page in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/wc-mac-sessiond/<id>`, so a restarted
service adopts running sessions and still releases them.

**Doorbells** (`sv_transport::vdoorbell`, `park`). An endpoint is one spelling
(`PortHandle::open`): `dev:NAME` (the guest's port: `/dev/virtio-ports/NAME` on
Linux, `/dev/NAME` on macOS, `\\.\Global\NAME` on Windows), `socket:PATH` (a
QEMU chardev or a hub's socket), `fd:R,W` (two inherited descriptors, role
(b)'s FIFO pair). A byte is a token:

| byte | meaning |
|---|---|
| `0x00`–`0x7F` | a lane: `slot << 1 \| lane` (`park::lane_token`) |
| `0xFC` `RESCAN_TOKEN` | rescan everything: a hub sends it to every client after (re)opening its port |
| `0xFD` | the Windows GPU pool's cold-path token (`COLD_TOKEN`, Windows branch) |
| `0xFE` `HELLO_TOKEN` | a guest's main process says a boot record waits (103.15) |

`BellTarget` has two required methods: `ring_token` and `rescan`. **The rescan
rule:** a byte sent while a port is closed is lost (Linux's `virtio_console`
drops bytes that arrive while no process has the port open; a hub's socket
drops what arrives while it restarts), so `serve_port` calls `rescan` on every
open and reopen and on `RESCAN_TOKEN`, and every waiter looks at its ring
again instead of trusting that it saw every wake. Tested
(`every_reopen_and_every_rescan_token_rescans`,
`a_rescan_ends_a_wait_whose_wake_was_lost`, the hub's
`clients_survive_the_upstream_reconnecting`). Waiting is
`ByteChannel::wait_readable(slice)`: the `Bell` handshake on the lane's own
word, which on macOS is `os_sync_wait_on_address` (public since 14.4, looked up
at run time).

**Clocks shared across sides.** On macOS a timestamp another side compares is
`mach_absolute_time()` scaled by `mach_timebase_info` (`frametrace::mono_us`),
never the raw counter: on Apple Silicon `cntfrq_el0` reads 1 GHz from user
space and `cntvct_el0` is not the 24 MHz counter, while `mach_absolute_time`
ticks at 24 MHz with timebase 125/3 and a Linux guest's counter tracks it to a
few hundred ticks (measured on the real Mac). Until 103.15, `mono_us` used
Linux's `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` id on every Unix, which is not a clock on macOS.

**Measured on the real Mac (role (b), libkrun, `wcbell`/`svbell`):** round trip
p50 46–57 µs, p99 114–170 µs, max 0.3–2.1 ms; one way, Mac to guest about
35–43 µs and guest to Mac about 5–17 µs; both bells passed 100 of 100 reopen
cycles.

The sound ring's stream protocol is 103.16.

### 103.15 No ssh at all, doorbells, damage-only surfaces, and the keeper

**(a) The bootstrap without ssh.** 103.14 left three ssh execs per main
process. They are gone, and so is the private sshd. The main process's
compositor writes a boot record into page 0 of its ring window (103.14.1) and
rings `HELLO_TOKEN` on the rings' doorbell, every 3 s until answered. On the
host, `wc-arena-host mac-sessiond` (user unit `wc-mac-sessiond`, installed by
`scripts/mac-launch-install.sh`) wakes on the hello, sweeps QEMU's memory
backend for page-0 stamps carrying a waiting record, runs `wc-session up`,
`rings` and `proxy`, and answers `Located` in the same page; the guest then
makes its control region. A refusal is `Failed` with `wc-session`'s reason,
which the launcher logs. The words reach `wc-session` as
`SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND`, so a record's fields meet exactly the forced command's
validation. Installing needs no channel either: the harness asks `wc-session
app` on the host and passes the answers to `wc-launch --install --meta DIR`.

* Measured: hello to record found 0.44–0.49 s (one 4 GiB sweep), both locates
  0.92–1.10 s, proxy started 1.5–1.8 s after the hello; the launcher's
  "session up" 2.0–2.3 s after the main process started (2.9–3.1 s with the GPU
  server). Without a doorbell the service sweeps on a timer (`--sweep-secs`),
  and a 2 s timer costs 17% of a host core: the hello is what makes the sweep
  rare.
* `down`: the proxy answers `ok down` (0.3 ms round trip) and exits; the
  service runs `wc-session down` when the unit has ended. A main process killed
  with `kill -9`: the lease ended the proxy in 6 s and the service took the
  session down.
* The GPU server starts the same way. With `gpu-server` (and `gpu-icd`,
  `gpu-bell`) in `wc-launch.ini`, the main process starts `sv-guest gpu guest
  --label <session>` and sets the record's GPU flag; the service runs
  `wc-session gpu`, whose guest-RAM branch starts `sv-hostd qemu-serve --cold
  mem:<label>` in the session's unit. `scripts/mac-gpu.sh` (default
  `MAC_GPU_VIA=session`) uses this path: main process opened to GPU served in
  2.9–3.1 s, three frames identical, no network socket on either side.
  `MAC_GPU_VIA=ssh` keeps 103.6's harness bootstrap for comparison.

**(b) Doorbells.** The VM has a legacy virtio-serial controller
(`disable-modern=on`) with two ports, `org.sirati.wcbell.0` and
`org.sirati.svbell.0`. macOS names them `/dev/cu.org.sirati.wcbell.0` and
`/dev/cu.org.sirati.svbell.0` (AppleVirtIOConsole's `IOTTYBaseName` is the
port's name). One hub on the host (`sv-hostd bell-hub`, user unit
`wc-mac-bell-hub`) holds both chardevs and serves `wl.sock` (the proxy and the
session service) and `sv.sock` (the session's ICDs). In the guest the main
process opens the Wayland port (`--wayland-rings` with the guest-RAM rings
names it) and a doorman thread turns its bytes into the compositor loop's wake
and the lanes' own words, so the launcher's control and sound threads sleep on
their lanes; the GPU server opens the other (`--bell dev:…`).

| idle Text Editor/Console, 30 s | polled (1 ms) | doorbell |
|---|---|---|
| Wayland round trip, 2000 × `wl_display_roundtrip` | p50 2.07 ms, p99 2.14 ms | **p50 0.248 ms, p99 0.322 ms** |
| main process in the VM | 8.1% of a vCPU | **3.0%** |
| proxy on the host | 1.9% of a core | **0.47%** |
| GPU present, 300 frames 256×256 (sv-icd park mean) | 0.54 ms/frame (0.223 ms) | 0.56 ms/frame (0.167 ms) |

(103.14's polled p50 of 1.06 ms was measured with Firefox open; the polled
row here is the same idle session as the doorbell row.) The GPU present is
bound by other costs at this size; the doorbell shortens the ICD's waits and
not the frame.

**(c) The copy into the IOSurface.** What public API allows:

* *Aliasing an IOSurface to the arena's pages:* not possible. `IOSurfaceCreate`
  allocates its own memory and has no property for an existing address (the
  14.5 SDK's keys were checked); `CVPixelBufferCreateWithBytes` wraps memory
  but such a buffer has no IOSurface (`CVPixelBufferGetIOSurface` is NULL);
  Metal's `newBufferWithBytesNoCopy` wraps it as a GPU buffer, which needs Metal
  (absent in this VM) and still ends in a blit into the layer's drawable.
* *The reverse, client buffers living in IOSurfaces:* each buffer would be its
  own region the host locates (a 4 GiB sweep, 0.45 s, per buffer), whose stride
  the client chose, and IOSurface memory is not documented as wired, which the
  locate needs. Not done.
* *Damage-only copies:* done. Each IOSurface of a window's pair keeps the damage
  it missed since it was last the back buffer (every present's damage goes to
  both); a present copies the back surface's list, or the whole window when
  that is more than half of it.

Measured, Console 1280×681 (`face-full-copy` in the support directory forces
whole copies for the comparison):

| 100 presents | whole window | damage only |
|---|---|---|
| typing | 349 MB, 0.21–0.23 ms per present | **19 MB (5.5%), 0.025 ms** |
| `seq 1 20000` scrolling | 370 MB, 0.335 ms | **78 MB (21%), 0.164 ms** |

GTK 4's GL renderer, through EGL on `wl_shm`, damages the whole window every
frame, so the Mac's GTK applications run with `GSK_RENDERER=cairo` (and Mesa's
EGL, never the RTX 5090) in `apps.ini`. The copy chain is now damage-only at
every step: client buffer to arena (proxy), arena to shadow (compositor), shadow
to IOSurface (main process).

**The keeper: a guest kernel panic, and its fix.** Killing the main process
three times while Console scrolled panicked the guest kernel three times:
`[data.kalloc.4096]: element modified after free`, the page full of
`0xff1c1c1e`, Console's background colour. macOS frees a dead process's wired
pages at once and reuses them; the proxy wrote pixels into them for the rest of
its 5 s lease. The keeper below was the initial fix. Its elapsed-time
release and bounded shutdown were also unsafe: §111.9.3 replaces them with
release-word-only retention and an unbounded safe shutdown wait. The bullets
below describe the historical keeper, not the current broker policy.

* While a keeper is installed (`wc_handle::arena::set_region_keeper`), every
  guest-RAM window the main process makes is a POSIX shared-memory object,
  wired by the main process and, before the host hears of it, mapped and wired
  by `wc-launch --keeper` too. The name is then unlinked. The keeper is not in
  the main process's process group and ignores SIGTERM and SIGHUP.
* When its stdin ends (the main process exited, however), the keeper waits for
  the release word in the boot page. The session service writes it after the
  proxy's and the GPU server's units have ended and `down` has run. Then the
  keeper kills the session's GPU server and exits, and only then are the pages
  free. With no release in 10 minutes it frees anyway.
* No keeper, no session: the main process refuses to start without one.
* A shutdown does not wait on it. The keeper first ignored SIGTERM, so every
  macOS shutdown waited until launchd killed it (the main process died on the
  signal without `down`, and the release came only after the 5 s lease). Now
  the main process answers SIGTERM with `down` over the control ring and exits,
  the host releases within about 1–2 s (measured 1.15 s), and a keeper that
  has seen SIGTERM waits at most 10 s. This VM's stops still leave a
  `shutdown_stall` report: macOS samples whatever is alive 2 s into the
  shutdown, Apple's own processes included, before our processes have had
  their SIGTERM.
* Measured: five kills under the same scrolling load, no panic (the panic count
  stayed at 3); each time the keeper held 70 MiB for about 6 s until the
  release.
* Not covered: the GPU server's own extent, if the GPU server itself crashes
  while `sv-hostd` serves it (it is killed only after the release in every
  other case), and a keeper killed with SIGKILL.

**The channels now** (role (a), this VM):

| channel | crosses as | copies |
|---|---|---|
| bootstrap | the boot record in page 0 of the ring window, found by the host's sweep after a hello on the doorbell | none; no ssh, no socket |
| Wayland bytes | ring slots in guest RAM, woken by the `wcbell` doorbell | proxy into the ring (1); compositor out of the ring into its local socket pair (1) |
| `wl_shm` frames | the arena in guest RAM | client damage into an arena slice (1); slice to shadow, damage (1); shadow to IOSurface, damage (1); face and Core Animation (0) |
| Vulkan | the GPU extent in guest RAM, cold path in its first page, `svbell` doorbell | as 103.6 |
| control, lease, `down` | the control slot, woken by the doorbell | a line each way |
| sound | the sound slot | 103.16 |
| clipboard, icons | their feed slots | as 103.14 |
| face to main | 0600 Unix socket inside macOS; IOSurfaces by mach port | pixels 0 |
| GPU server start | the main process, flagged in the boot record; `sv-hostd` started by the session service | none |

Evidence: `/mnt/datasets/builds/evidence/macos-zero-copy/` (`rtt-*.txt`,
`*-cpu-*.txt`, `gpu-bell-ab.txt`, `copy-ab.txt`, `sound-tone.txt`,
`macgpu-last/`, `text-editor.png`), outside the repository.

### 103.16 The sound ring: every device a stream, both directions, credit not drops

103.14's sound was one stream, Linux to Mac, and the proxy dropped a chunk
whenever the ring was full. It is now a general transport
(`sv_transport::soundring`), meant to replace the real Mac's system-wide
PulseAudio tunnels over vsock and to carry Windows' sound too. It runs on the
`OWNER_AUDIO` slot, one byte channel for every stream.

**The stream protocol** (version 1). Frames, little-endian: an 8-byte header
(`type u8`, `flags u8` = 0, `stream u16`, `len u32`) and `len` bytes, at most
64 KiB.

| type | from | payload |
|---|---|---|
| `0x01 Hello` | both | `u32 version` |
| `0x10 Device` | device side | `u8 dir` (0 output, 1 input), `u8 channels`, `u8 format` (1 = s16le), `u8 0`, `u32 rate`, the device's name (UTF-8) |
| `0x11 Gone` | device side | none |
| `0x12 Default` | device side | `u8 dir`; `stream` is now that direction's default |
| `0x20 Data` | both | PCM, interleaved, the stream's format: output streams session to device, input streams device to session |
| `0x21 Credit` | both | `u32` bytes more the `Data` sender may send on `stream` |
| `0x22 Start` | session side | capture this input stream (something records from it) |
| `0x23 Stop` | session side | stop capturing it |

The **device side** is the machine with the speakers and microphones (the
Mac); the **session side** is the Linux applications' sound server. A stream
id names one device and one direction for as long as that device exists; ids
are not reused. After a `Device` for an output, the device side grants what its
queue holds (`Credit`) and grants again as it plays; after a `Device` for an
input, the session side grants. `Data` beyond the credit is a protocol error.
An unknown type is skipped by its length, so a later version can add messages.
Capture runs only between `Start` and `Stop`, so a microphone is open only
while something records. `soundring::spawn` is the one thread that owns the
channel on either side: it writes what other threads queue in order, waits out
a full ring without dropping and without ceasing to read (so credit still
arrives), and is woken by `Link::send` through the lane's own word (a
`Kicker`).

**Backpressure, end to end.** On the session side an output stream is
`module-pipe-sink` writing into a FIFO the proxy reads. A pipe sink is paced
by its reader. When the Mac has granted nothing, the proxy does not read, the
FIFO fills, the sink stops, and the Linux application's stream waits. Nothing
is dropped anywhere between the application and the speaker. An input stream is
`module-pipe-source` reading from a FIFO the proxy writes the Mac's recording
into; the proxy grants 32 KiB at a time, as the FIFO takes it. A microphone
cannot wait, so what the Mac records beyond its credit is counted as an
overrun, never queued.

**Devices and defaults.** The Mac side (`wc-launch/src/sound_mac.rs`) lists
CoreAudio's devices once a second. Each output gets its own AudioQueue bound to
the device's UID (`kAudioQueueProperty_CurrentDevice`); each input gets a
recorder started on `Start`. It announces the default output and input as they
change, and the proxy makes them the session's (`pactl set-default-sink`,
`set-default-source`), so the Linux applications follow the Mac's choice. The
sinks are named `wc_mac_out_<n>` and `wc_mac_in_<n>`, described by the Mac's
device names. An output idle for 3 s is paused.

**The session's server.**
* `WC_LAUNCH_AUDIO=on` (the default): a PulseAudio of the session's own, as
  before. Its pipe sinks suspend on idle (`module-suspend-on-idle`), so no
  silence crosses the ring.
* `WC_LAUNCH_AUDIO_NULL_SINK=off`: no null sink and no monitor socket; the
  ring's devices are the session's only ones.
* `WC_LAUNCH_AUDIO=system`: no server of the session's own. The applications
  use this user's PipeWire or PulseAudio and its default sink
  (`PULSE_SERVER` points at it), and the proxy adds the Mac's devices to that
  server; `wc-session down` unloads them (`sound.modules`). This is the mode for
  a guest whose PipeWire already provides devices.
* The single-stream path (`--audio-socket`, raw PCM on `OWNER_AUDIO`) remains
  for the Windows launcher until it adopts this protocol.

**The microphone and TCC.** Recording needs the user's permission, which macOS
asks for on the first `AudioQueueStart` of an input. The main process is started
by a face, so TCC attributes it to that application's bundle, and every bundle's
`Info.plist` now carries `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription`. **Not tested:** this
VM's only sound device is QEMU's `usb-audio`, which has no input, so no input
stream exists here, and no capture or permission prompt was seen.

**Measured** (the VM, Console's session, QEMU's `wav` audiodev recording the
VM's output): 5.000 s of a 440 Hz tone played with `pacat` into
`wc_mac_out_1` came out as 5.000 s at 439.9 Hz with no gap of 5 ms or more.
103.14's single stream lost 90 ms in 6 s and dropped chunks on a full ring.

**A ring bug found on the way** (`sv_transport::ring`). A packet that does not
fit before the lane's end makes the producer publish a pad to the end and start
over at zero. If the packet still did not fit, the producer returned `RingFull`
having published the pad without ringing the bell, so a consumer asleep on the
lane never read the pad, and the producer saw `RingFull` for ever. Any writer
of near-capacity packets facing a parked reader could hit it; the sound ring's
64 KiB frames did at once. The pad now rings the bell
(`a_pad_wakes_a_parked_reader` fails without it). In the same work, a channel
thread's sleep now compares against the lane's wake count taken before it
looked at its queue (`ByteChannel::wake_epoch`, `wait_readable_since`), so a
`Kicker::kick` between the two is not slept through.

### 103.17 Role (b): a Mac hosting the Linux VM boots as the Windows guest does

In role (b) the Mac runs the compositor and the Linux VM (libkrun on
Hypervisor.framework) runs the applications. There is no guest RAM to sweep:
the shared memory is one file on a Mac RAM disk, which the hypervisor shares
into the guest through a virtio-fs DAX window (`/run/host-shm/arena` there),
so both sides map the same pages. That is the ivshmem layout of §83 and §89 on
a different substrate, and the boot is §105's, with the roles of the two
sides the same as on Windows: the Mac is the side with the compositor.

**Mac (`wc-launch`, `mac.rs`).** `arena-file = PATH` in `wc-launch.ini` (or
`WC_MAC_ARENA_STANDIN`) selects role (b). The main process then

* maps the file as ivshmem device 0 (`WC_IVSHMEM_STANDIN`, `--arena-ivshmem 0`)
  and keeps the Wayland rings in its tail, not in a guest-RAM window;
* opens the hypervisor's FIFO pair for the rings' virtio-serial port
  (`wayland-bell = PREFIX`: `PREFIX.from-guest`, `PREFIX.to-guest`, both
  read-write so neither open waits on the other side) and passes it as
  `fd:R,W` (`ringlink::open_bell_port` takes §105.4's prefixed spellings);
* passes `--boot-session/--boot-install/--boot-key/--control-socket`
  (`plan::boot_argv`), so `session_svc` writes the signed record into the
  header page, rings `HELLO_TOKEN`, and holds the control ring and the lease;
* sends its requests (`run`, `down`) through that control socket, and plays
  and records the sound ring itself (§103.16, every CoreAudio device), so
  `--session-audio` is not passed.

**Guest.** `wc-arena-host sessiond --arena-file /run/host-shm/arena --installs
DIR --bell HUB/wl.sock`, a user unit beside `sv-hostd bell-hub --port
dev:org.sirati.wcbell.0=HUB/wl.sock` (§99, the hub holding the guest's own
port). The installation is a writable directory holding a link to
`wc-session` and `session.key`, made on the service's first start; deploy
copies the key to the Mac's support directory (mode 0600). `wc-session`'s
ivshmem check wants a socket at `$WC_LAUNCH_WCBELL`; in a guest that is the
hub's `wl.sock` (and `$WC_LAUNCH_BELL` its `sv.sock`).

**Run (an A18 Mac, macOS 26, foot from the guest).** Hello to `located` 0.72 s
(the guest's `up` 0.21 s, the proxy 0.5 s). Control requests answered in
1.4–5 ms, which is the verb's own work in `wc-session`, not the ring. The sound
ring announced both outputs and the microphone and followed the defaults.
foot's window took focus and pointer input. Nothing crossed but the arena and
the bell port: no ssh, socket, TCP or vsock in the session's path.

**Found on the way.**

* An application that asks for a `wl_shm` pool larger than the arena's
  largest run is not refused cleanly. The proxy holds the pool back and
  absorbs every request naming it, including the `create_pool` itself, so the
  compositor's object ids fall out of step and the client dies on
  `Invalid new_id`. foot reserves 512 MiB pools by default (scrolling by
  offset); `-o tweak.max-shm-pool-size-mb=0` avoids it in a 128 MiB arena.
* The proxy's microphone source failed to load (`mkfifo sound-2.fifo: File
  exists`) once the Mac's devices were re-announced.

### 103.18 Output scale: Retina without blur

Until this section every surface pixel was one Mac point, and on a Retina
screen AppKit doubled the layer: correct and soft (103.7's table). Now the one
output has an integer scale S, which the platform gives (`Started::scale`):
the main screen's `backingScaleFactor`, rounded, at least 1, on macOS; 1 on
Win32 and headless. `--output-scale N` overrides it, for a harness. It is read
through `State::scale_for(surface)`, so a platform with a scale per monitor
(Windows' per-monitor DPI) changes that function and the output setup, not the
readers.

**Logical stays logical.** Configure sizes, window geometry, input, pointer
constraints, popup placement, `ToUi::Map`/`Resize`/`MovePopup` and the
control socket's rectangles are in surface units, which are Mac points. Only
pixels are in device pixels.

**What a client sees at S > 1:**

| | S = 1 (unchanged) | S > 1 |
|---|---|---|
| `wl_output.mode` | logical size | logical size × S |
| `wl_output.scale` | not sent (1) | S |
| `wl_compositor` | version 5 | version 6 |
| `wl_surface.preferred_buffer_scale` | never | S, at `new_surface` |
| a buffer of scale B ≠ 1 | drawn unscaled, and logged | honoured |

**Pixels.** A surface's staging shadow, and so a window's shadow, is its
logical size × S. A buffer with B = S is copied 1:1. Any other B is a view
(`surface::view_of`, §102's path): the whole buffer resampled, nearest
neighbour, to (buffer / B) × S, which is ×2 for an Xwayland or other B = 1
client on S = 2. A viewport's destination is logical, so it is × S as well.
Surface damage is mapped into buffer pixels (× B), buffer damage into the
shadow by the view (S / B, widened by a pixel), and subsurface offsets (× S)
when the tree is composed. Readers that want a size (bounds, hit test,
pointer holds, the geometry-only commit, `mapped_windows`) divide by S
(`State::surface_size`). The shadow carries its scale (`Shadow::scale`), so
the platform knows how many points it is.

**macOS.** The layer's `contentsScale` is set to the shadow's scale on every
present, since AppKit resets it when a window changes screen; window and popup
frames already come from logical sizes. The face's IOSurface pair is the
shadow's size in pixels, and `ToFace::Surface` carries the scale. A client
cursor's `NSImage` is sized in points (`image / B`, `CursorSpec::Image.scale`),
with the hotspot in points; Win32 ignores the scale, as before.

**Checked here (Linux, headless, `--output-scale 2`).** weston-terminal
(version 5, told by `wl_output.scale` and `enter`) drew at B = 2 into a
1484x854 shadow for a 742x427 window, after a first B = 1 frame that was
doubled; foot (version 6) read `preferred_buffer_scale(2)` before its first
frame; weston-presentation-shm stayed at B = 1 and was doubled. At S = 1
weston-terminal's frame hashes were those of the binary before this section.
The macOS half (`contentsScale`, the cursor's size, popup frames on a Retina
screen) was compiled, not run.

**Not built.** Fractional scale (`wp_fractional_scale_v1` with viewporter,
for 125 % and 150 %), which this does not design out: the scale is per output
and the view path already resamples. A scale that changes while running (a
window moved to a screen of another scale): S is read once at start. Windows'
per-monitor DPI. A filter better than nearest neighbour for B ≠ S.

### 103.12 Not built, and not proven

* **Not built.** Drag and drop in either direction. IME and dead keys beyond
  what XKB composes in the client (no `NSTextInputClient`, no `text-input-v3`).
  Fractional scale (integer Retina scale is 103.18). SVG icons (the host's resolver
  has no renderer, as on Windows). A frequent-pages section in the Dock menu
  (`macbundle::dock_items` takes them, and the launcher does not fetch
  `frequent` yet).
* **Role (b), a Mac hosting a Linux VM, is designed and not built.** That
  covers 103.5's QEMU+HVF `memory-backend-shm` arena, the Linux guest mapping
  BAR2, and the Virtualization.framework variant.
* **Real Metal.** Nothing here ran on a Metal device. MoltenVK was shown to
  refuse cleanly without one. KosmicKrisp needs Apple Silicon and macOS 26.
* **Doorbells on macOS** are attached since 103.15 (two legacy virtio-serial
  ports, a hub on the host). A VM without them polls, at 103.15's measured cost.
* **Firefox's own sound.** The route was proven with a tone played into the
  session's sink. A tone Firefox opened from `file://` did not play. Firefox
  appears to want a gesture for a media document, and this was not chased.
* **Superpages at 4 GiB.** A 4 GiB macOS guest has none (103.3). Every result
  above is on wired 4 KiB pages. Superpages were only seen at 8 and 12 GiB.
* **Cooperative activation.** macOS 14 does not let a process that started
  outside LaunchServices take the foreground from the active application. A
  bundle opened from the Dock or with `open` is activated; `mac-window.sh`'s
  bare compositor can open behind the frontmost window.
* **One known `sv-icd` bug**, found here and not macOS's: with the default
  pipelined headless present, the frame dump for frame N holds frame N+1's
  pixels. It reproduces on Linux with RADV and no VM.


## 104. KWin composites on the guest's GPU: a userspace render node, and frames that are never copied

2026-10-19, branch `kwin-gpu` (with `kwin-gpu-drm`, `kwin-gpu-proxy` and
`kwin-gpu-icd` merged into it), and nix-config branch `testhost-kwin-gpu`
(from `testhost-win7-nested`). The goal: the nested KWin of §102 composites
with OpenGL on the forwarded GPU instead of QPainter, so that Aero glass works
and the frames stop being drawn by the host's CPU.

### 104.1 Status in one paragraph

**Works on the real guest.** KWin reports `Compositing Type: OpenGL` with
`OpenGL renderer string: zink Vulkan 1.4(Intel(R) UHD Graphics
(INTEL_PROPRIETARY_WINDOWS))`, and the Aero glass blur effect (`aeroglassblur`)
is loaded and visible: the taskbar's view of the wallpaper is blurred under
OpenGL and sharp under QPainter (104.8). KWin renders into LINEAR images that
live in named sections the guest's GPU process creates; the compositor maps
those sections and reads KWin's pixels from them. **Nothing copies a frame:**
1200 of 1200 commits in 20 s reached the compositor this way, and the proxy
copied 0 bytes, against 300 MB in the same 20 s under QPainter. Both paths
hold 60 frames a second. The CPU cost is not lower yet: with these light
workloads KWin takes 16–17 % of a host core against 6–8 %, and the guest's
compositor and GPU side together take about 55 % of a guest core against
16–20 % (104.8). No driver fault on the guest. Locally, two NixOS VM tests
pass on lavapipe.

### 104.2 The decision: a userspace render node, sections, no kernel driver

KWin 6.7's nested backend offers OpenGL only when the host compositor names a
render node in `zwp_linux_dmabuf_v1` feedback and KWin can open it
(`WaylandBackend::supportedCompositors`, `wayland_backend.cpp`). It then
allocates its output buffers with GBM on that node, imports them as EGLImages,
and hands them to the host as dma-bufs. KWin has no Vulkan renderer, and its
EGL backend has no path without GBM (`wayland_egl_backend.cpp`).

The brief listed three ways; the user chose the second and ruled out kernel
drivers (no vgem, no udmabuf) and any copy:

| option | what | why not / why |
|---|---|---|
| (a) vgem + Mesa GBM | a real kernel render node, shmem dma-bufs | a kernel driver; and the dma-buf's pages are host shmem, so every frame would be copied from the guest's GPU memory into them and again into the compositor's arena |
| (b) userspace node | a CUSE character device answering the DRM ioctls Mesa and KWin issue; the "dma-bufs" are tokens naming guest-side memory | **chosen**: no kernel code, and the memory can be anything we choose |
| (c) a KWin patch | `wl_egl_window` and kopper, or a readback to `wl_shm` | a downstream KWin; and both paths read the frame back to the host |

**Where the frames live is decided by one fact of the guest.** The GPU
process and the compositor are separate processes, and each ivshmem device's
driver gives its BAR to one handle (§83.5, §87.2): the GPU process holds the
GPU pool, the compositor the arena. So KWin's buffers cannot be pool memory the
compositor reads. Both processes are children of `wc-launch.exe` in the same
Windows session, though, so they can share a **named, pagefile-backed
section**: the GPU process creates it, maps it and imports the view with
`VK_EXT_external_memory_host`; the compositor opens it by name. Nothing
crosses the VM boundary but the name (docs/design.md §1a); the host never maps
these pages, and they are not on any ivshmem device, which the rule for GPU
memory (dynamic, on ivshmem) is about memory the two sides share. Locally the
GPU side is a Linux process and the "section" is a file in `/dev/shm`, which
the compositor under Wine maps by its path.

Before any of it was built, `sv-extimg-probe` asked the guest's Intel driver
(Windows, 0x195ba4) the one question the design rests on, query first and each
riskier step opt-in: B8G8R8A8/R8G8B8A8 LINEAR with `HOST_ALLOCATION` is
IMPORTABLE; a section view imports as a host pointer (memory type bits 0x6);
a 1280×800 external LINEAR image needs type bits 0x7, row pitch 5120; a clear
and a render-pass clear land in the section exactly as the CPU reads them back.
(Output: `/mnt/datasets/builds/evidence/kwin-gpu/extimg-probe-guest.txt`.)

### 104.3 The render node: `sv-drm`

`crates/sv-drm`, one binary with two halves.

* **`sv-drm serve`** (root): a CUSE device (`/dev/cuse`, the FUSE kernel
  protocol, libc only), `DEVNAME=dri/renderD128`, dynamic major, minor 128, so
  devtmpfs creates `/dev/dri/renderD128`; then owner, group and mode as told.
  It answers `VERSION` (`svdrm`, with CUSE's retry dance for the string
  buffers), `GET_CAP` (PRIME import and export, no syncobj, no dumb buffers),
  `PRIME_FD_TO_HANDLE` (reads the caller's fd through `/proc/<pid>/fd`, only
  a regular tmpfs file, so a FIFO or this node cannot stall it; one GEM handle
  per token nonce per open), `GEM_CLOSE`, `GET_UNIQUE`; `PRIME_HANDLE_TO_FD`
  cannot work through CUSE (a server cannot put an fd into its caller), and
  nothing on this path needs it. KMS ioctls get `EOPNOTSUPP`.
* **`sv-drm ns`** (the user): a user and mount namespace in which libdrm sees
  that device as a render node on bus `faux`. libdrm checks
  `/sys/dev/char/M:m/device/drm`, the `subsystem` link's basename and
  `access("/dev/dri/renderD<minor>")`; a read-only tmpfs over
  `/sys/dev/char` holds every original link plus a small fake device tree.
  The process then drops back to its real ids in a nested user namespace and
  execs. It also mounts a private `/tmp/.X11-unix`: in the namespace the
  host's root-owned directory shows as the overflow uid, and
  `kwin_wayland_wrapper` refused to start Xwayland there.
  A device node bound into a tmpfs made inside a user namespace cannot be
  opened (measured: `EACCES`), which is why the node itself is the real
  `/dev/dri/renderD128` and only sysfs is faked.

**The dma-buf is a sealed memfd** (`sv_drm::token`): a header (magic, size,
the GPU side's 16-byte nonce, the section's name), the file sized to the
allocation, all four seals. Readers `pread` the header and refuse anything
unsealed; nothing maps it. Mesa's implicit-sync ioctls on it fail with ENOTTY,
which release builds ignore.

### 104.4 sv-icd and the GPU side

Only with `SV_DRM_NODE` set (the nested KWin's environment); everything else
is unchanged.

* **The ICD** advertises `VK_KHR_external_memory_fd`,
  `VK_EXT_external_memory_dma_buf`, `VK_EXT_image_drm_format_modifier` (LINEAR
  only), `VK_EXT_queue_family_foreign`, `VK_EXT_physical_device_drm` (the
  node's major and minor, which is how Zink matches the device to the fd) and
  `VK_KHR_external_semaphore_fd`, implements them itself and strips them from
  what the GPU side sees. A modifier image becomes a LINEAR one, a DMA_BUF image
  a HOST_ALLOCATION one; an exportable allocation is `svAllocShared`, an
  imported token `svImportShared`; `vkGetMemoryFdKHR` makes a new token.
  FOREIGN and EXTERNAL queue families become IGNORED in barriers.
* **Implicit sync, emulated:** Zink exports a SYNC_FD semaphore after every
  flush that touched an exported image; exporting submits a wait on it with a
  fence and waits for the fence, then returns -1 ("already signalled"). So when
  KWin's frame reaches the proxy, the GPU has finished it. An imported SYNC_FD
  drops the next wait on that semaphore, so the guest's GPU never waits on a
  semaphore nobody signals.
* **The GPU side** creates the section (`CreateFileMappingW`, named
  `Local\sv-shared-<pid>-<n>-<nonce>`; a `/dev/shm` file on Linux), imports the
  view into the session's device with the memory type the image and the host
  pointer have in common (type 1 on Intel), and only opens names it created,
  with the nonce checked. Before creating a HOST_ALLOCATION image it asks the
  driver whether that LINEAR image is importable, and refuses with
  `VK_ERROR_FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED` otherwise: Intel is never sent a combination
  it said it does not support.
* `SV_DEVICE_TYPE` (tests): the device type the ICD reports, because Mesa
  26.2's Zink rejects a CPU device (the ICD over lavapipe) unless
  `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE`, which would also put EGL on swrast.

### 104.5 The proxy: dma-bufs become sections, with nothing copied

`wc-proxy --dmabuf-node PATH` (wc-session: `$BASE/dmabuf-node`, written by
the deploy step from `WC_LAUNCH_DMABUF_NODE`). The node is checked per client,
because the seat creates it after the proxy started. The proxy itself owns a
`zwp_linux_dmabuf_v1` v4 global: feedback (ARGB/XRGB8888 LINEAR, main device
the node), params, `create_immed`. A buffer is checked against its token and
sent upstream as a `wl_shm` pool whose descriptor is `Section{name}` (or
`SharedFile{path}` locally) plus `create_buffer`. The compositor already maps
both, so it needed no change for the buffers. Every commit of such a buffer is
traced as `px.commit … copied=0 zero_copy=1`. Non-immediate `create` answers
`failed` (KWin and Mesa use `create_immed`).

Two fixes the OpenGL backend needed elsewhere: the compositor refused KWin's
second `place_above` (its five layer subsurfaces are stacked before one
commit, and §68's staged order was a snapshot that did not know the new
sibling); and the GPU side called `vkGetCalibratedTimestampsKHR` through the
loader's trampoline on a driver that has only the EXT entry point.

### 104.6 The NixOS side

nix-config `testhost-kwin-gpu`:

* `nestedTest.kwinGpu`: with a GPU offered by the launcher, the seat runs
  `sv-drm serve` (vendored as `win7-desktop/sv-drm`, built in the system, so
  root runs the system's binary) for group `users`, mode 0660, and KWin's
  drop-in runs `kwin_wayland_wrapper` inside `sv-drm ns` with the ICD's
  environment only (`VK_DRIVER_FILES`, `SV_SOCKET`, `SV_BELL`), `SV_DRM_NODE`,
  `KWIN_RENDER_NODES`, `MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE=zink`,
  `KWIN_DISABLE_VULKAN=1` and `KWIN_NO_TIMER_QUERY=1` (a render-time query
  per frame is a GPU round trip, and its query copy took lavapipe down).
* The seat accepts `SV_DEVICE_TYPE`; `atp-nested` leaves out wc-session's
  preloaded Wayland shim, which is not in the store and would end the seat.
* `windows-vm`'s `waycomposeArena.gpu.users`: a named ACL on the GPU region
  alone (not the arena, not the doorbells) for users whose own processes load
  sv-icd; testhost sets `<desktop-user>`. Applied live once with `setfacl`; the VM's
  next start applies it from the configuration.
* testhost: `gpuForwarding` and `kwinGpu` on. Switched after `dry-activate`
  (polkit and home-manager-<desktop-user> restarted, windows-vm not).
* The deploy step: `WC_LAUNCH_ICD_STORE=1` puts the ICD with a manifest that
  names it relatively into the host's store (the seat passes only store paths
  to another user), `WC_LAUNCH_DMABUF_NODE`; `linux-desktop` has `gpu = on`.

| `win7-desktop/tests/nested-kwin-gpu.nix` (KWin alone, lavapipe, Wine, 2 GiB) | CUSE node `243:128`; EGL on GBM inside the namespace: `zink Vulkan 1.4(llvmpipe …)`; KWin "OpenGL compositing has been successfully initialized"; 1200 zero-copy commits in 20 s (60/s) with an animating client, 0 copied |
| `win7-desktop/tests/nested-waycompose-gpu.nix` (the Aero session through `atp-nested` with `kwinGpu`, 3 GiB; 1.7 GiB used at the peak) | `Compositing Type: OpenGL`, renderer `zink … (MESA_LLVMPIPE)`, `aeroglassblur` loaded; 102 zero-copy commits in 20 s of pointer motion, 0 copied |

### 104.8 On the guest

2026-10-19, 12:28–12:55, under the lease, the desktop idle (it had been
locked for hours; unlocked once with the PIN and locked again at the end).
Installation `wclinux` deployed with `WC_LAUNCH_GPU_SESSIONS=4` (all passed:
`/mnt/datasets/builds/evidence/kwin-gpu/deploy-104.txt`); the session started
in the interactive session as the shortcut does (`wc-launch.exe
linux-desktop`), autologin armed by root. The animating client was
`weston-presentation-shm` (and `eglgears_wayland -fullscreen` on llvmpipe as a
second), started in <desktop-user>'s session; each run 20 s.

| | QPainter (gpu off) | OpenGL on Zink (gpu on) |
|---|---|---|
| KWin's `supportInformation` | `Compositing Type: QPainter` | `Compositing Type: OpenGL`, renderer `zink Vulkan 1.4(Intel(R) UHD Graphics (INTEL_PROPRIETARY_WINDOWS))`, OpenGL 4.3 core, Driver Intel |
| commits reaching the compositor | 59/s | 59–60/s, every one zero-copy |
| bytes the proxy copied in 20 s | 300 MB (presentation-shm), 479 MB (gears) | **0** |
| host CPU, % of one core: KWin / proxy / sv-hostd | 6–8 / 3 / 0 | 16–17 / 1 / 0 |
| host CPU, all cores busy | 7–8 % | 12–14 % |
| guest: compositor / GPU side, % of one core | 16–20 / 0 | 34–35 / 20–25 |
| <desktop-user>'s slice / host available | 1.14–1.19 GB / 2.16–2.19 GiB | 1.39–1.45 GB / 1.86–1.92 GiB |
| Aero glass (taskbar) | tinted, wallpaper behind it sharp | frosted: wallpaper blurred (neighbour-pixel difference 0.77 against 3.0) |

The pictures were judged by a separate agent (`gl.png`, `qp.png` in
`/mnt/datasets/builds/evidence/kwin-gpu/guest/`): both drawn correctly, no
artifacts, the blur present only under OpenGL. Xwayland runs in the OpenGL
session (after the `/tmp/.X11-unix` fix). The GPU process's log shows the
sections (`Local\sv-shared-8056-1-…`, 3536 KiB, type 1); no `igvk64.dll`
fault, no Display or dxgkrnl event.

**Why the CPU is higher, as far as measured.** These workloads repaint little:
QPainter redraws only the damaged rectangle and the proxy copies only that.
Under OpenGL, KWin's thread pays Zink and the ICD's encoding for every frame
and waits, once per frame, for the guest's GPU (the SYNC_FD export); the
compositor reads the whole 1264×713 section at every commit instead of a
damaged slice; and the GPU side now has work. A heavy repaint (a maximised
window moving, effects across the screen) is where the GPU should win, and it
was not measured.

| `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` | 3092 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p sv-drm -p wc-proxy -p sv-icd -p sv-gpu-server --all-targets` | no warning in a line this branch wrote |
